Reseña: Brevard Zoo Calificación: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5) Es un lugar sorprendente y una opción excelente para ir en familia. El zoológico es grande y cuenta con una gran variedad de animales muy bien cuidados. Como hay que caminar bastante, el parque está muy bien pensado: ofrecen zonas con ventiladores y áreas con chorros de agua para refrescarte durante todo el recorrido, lo cual se agradece muchísimo. Aquí les dejo algunos detalles importantes sobre los precios y la experiencia: Precios de entrada y parqueo: El costo fue de $40 dólares por dos adultos y $14 dólares por mi hijo de 4 años. Un gran punto a favor es que el estacionamiento es gratis. El paseo en tren: Tienen un pequeño tren que sale cada cierto tiempo y cuesta $6 dólares por persona. Te da una pequeña vuelta por una zona dentro de una jaula grande donde tienen animales que no son peligrosos. En mi opinión, no vale la pena pagarlo, ya que caminando puedes ver absolutamente todo, incluyendo esa misma zona por donde pasa el tren. Comida y bebida: Recomiendo llevar agua y calzado muy cómodo para la caminata. Ellos permiten entrar con agua (y creo que también comida). Adentro hay opciones para comprar, pero los precios son bastante altos. Consejo clave: Si estás pensando ir apenas una hora antes de que cierren, no te va a dar tiempo de ver todas las cosas y exhibiciones que ofrecen. Es muchísimo mejor llegar temprano para disfrutarlo con calma. ¡Una experiencia buenísima que sin duda repetiremos!

It was only around 8:45, roughly an hour before closing. It's a shame because the kitchen is producing food that's good enough to bring people back again and again. I just wish the front-of-house staff showed the same level of care and attention as the people preparing the food.

We checked in with the hostess desk and were added to the waitlist, which ended up being very accurate. The hostess also asked for our seating preference (indoor, outdoor, or high-top), which was appreciated. Our party of three started with the original Domu wings and the tako. For entrées, we ordered the green curry ramen, Richie Rich ramen, and the wagyu Sichuan mazemen. The Domu wings were double-fried in a style similar to Korean fried chicken, with a sweet and salty flavor profile. They were crispy and enjoyable overall. 7/10 The tako was well dressed and had a bright, refreshing flavor from the mint. 8/10 The spicy green curry ramen had a strong curry flavor with a nice brightness to the broth, though it wasn’t very spicy. I personally would have preferred more Thai-style heat, but I wanted to try the broth as-is without adding the chili bomb. The noodles had a great texture, and while I think coconut milk could have added a creamier depth, the dish was still well executed. 8/10 The Richie Rich ramen had a fairly standard pork broth with a noticeable garlic kick, but nothing particularly memorable. 6/10 The wagyu sichuan mazemen, a dry noodle dish, was the biggest disappointment. The flavor felt lackluster, and the meat had a gritty texture that wasn’t what we expected from wagyu. It also lacked the spice and signature numbing sensation typically associated with Sichuan dishes. Overall, the service was great, and all of the food came out hot and fresh. While the…

From the moment you sit down and those hot, golden corn fritters hit the table, you know you're in for something special. They're complimentary, addictive, and the perfect way to kick off a meal. The rock shrimp are legendary for a reason — sweet, tender, and cooked to perfection. You can tell the seafood is fresh; sourced right from Port Canaveral, it shows in every bite. I ordered the shrimp combo and couldn't stop eating. Portions are generous without feeling excessive. The atmosphere is warm and unpretentious — exactly what a classic Florida seafood restaurant should be. The staff was friendly and attentive, making the whole experience feel welcoming from start to finish. If you're visiting the Space Coast or passing through Titusville, this place is a must. It's been a staple since 1983 and it's easy to see why. Highly recommend!

This was, without question, the worst experience I have ever had at a DoubleTree property. What was most disappointing was not just the error itself, but the complete lack of accountability and customer care shown afterward. At no point was there any effort to acknowledge the inconvenience or make the situation right. A hotel’s true measure of service is how it responds when something goes wrong. Unfortunately, DoubleTree failed in that regard. This experience left me extremely dissatisfied, and as a result, I will not choose to stay at a DoubleTree property again, nor will I recommend the brand to others. The food was great. They were very slow, but they were doing a new roll out on tablets for ordering and paying. Got lost in the shuffle, but once they get that in order, will only take a day, love this place!

Best Breakfast Spot in Orlando If you’re looking for a place that feels like home the second you walk through the door, Dixie Belle’s Cafe is it. From the friendly staff to the incredible food, everything about this place screams Southern hospitality. The portions are huge, the prices are fair, and every bite tastes like it was made from scratch. The biscuits are some of the best I’ve ever had, the grits are perfectly cooked, and the breakfast plates come out hot, fresh, and loaded with flavor. You can tell they genuinely care about the quality of their food and their customers. What really sets Dixie Belle’s apart is the atmosphere. It feels like a local favorite for a reason—everyone is treated like family. Even when they’re busy, the staff keeps a smile on their face and makes sure you’re taken care of. I’ve eaten breakfast all over the country, and Dixie Belle’s is the kind of place that makes you wish you had one back home. If you’re visiting Orlando or live nearby, do yourself a favor and stop in. You’ll leave full, happy, and already planning your next visit. 10/10. Worth every minute of the wait. 🍳🥓☕️❤️
First time eating here, nice atmosphere very friendly service, home cooked meals great prices. All around very nice business, definitely recommend eating here.

Okay, I'm a sucker for Southern Comfort Food and places that make you feel like you are a regular even if you've never been there before. Places that, if you were a regular, you'd surely know everyone there by name. The food is extremely good. The service is absolutely some of the most friendly and accommodating I've ever experienced. The atmosphere is a cafe/dinner; clean, hospitable, and with just enough southern charm to be authentic without falling into the trap of becoming a theme restaurant. I had the Rueben and fries, the Rueben was cheesy with that slap-on-the-tongue sour kraut tang, the corned beef was spot on with just enough dressing to keep the flavors flowing without taking over the whole sandwich. The fries were homestyle with a crispy outside and a tender interior; just like a cloud... a fluffy deep fried cloud. I finished off my lunch with peach cobbler, it was creamy, peachy, and completely authentic... I absolutely love Dixie Belle's and make a point of going there every time I am in Orlando. Thanks "Y'all" for a great dining experience... (see you for breakfast!)!!!
Great local gem!!! I was visiting a friend in Orlando and she mentioned Dixie Belle for breakfast. It was delicious! We arrived ~830am and had no wait, but the place was packed when we left!

My husband and I got the oceanfront 2 room suite with balcony on the 8th floor and could not have been more pleased. The room was clean and I felt comfortable using the cleaned dresser drawers. We stayed five nights and saved money making use of the mini fridge and microwave. The beds were comfortable and we enjoyed listening to the waves crashing onto the shore at night from the room. The nighttime view from the balcony of the moon over the ocean was breathtaking. We had an added bonus of seeing two rocket launches from our balcony during our stay, as well. The beach was a very short distance with access directly from the pool area. We rented the full set cabana two days. We stayed Sunday through Friday and could see that there are many more people on the weekends so weekdays were much quieter. I highly recommend staying here. Hilton never disappoints.

Clean rooms with a great view. We were in double bed with separate couch suite. The pool was good. They do have beach service that you can rent chairs and umbrella all day for $40. It can be charged to your room if you do not want to bring cash. Lots of restaurants in a short drive. The beach was quiet and away from the chaos of Daytona beach. Compared to Daytona, that is still recovering from the past hurricanes, everything here is operational and a lot less expensive. The staff were kind and accommodating. The pool is smaller and tends to get crowded quickly. Down on the beach you can rent 2 chairs and umbrella all day for $40 (“all day” ends at 5pm). The rooms are spacious, and the bed was amazingly comfortable. However- the sliding door to the balcony almost took 2 of us to slide open. Elevators are quick! The food stands out also- we had a burger at the tiki bar as well as coconut shrimp and both were quite tasty! Last but certainly not least I got the pleasure to speaking to the manger Greg just to make sure he knew how grateful I was for his staff being on their toes and easily understand why they’ve been there for so long working because it’s exactly the type of environment you want to be in for work. Not so short but definitely sweet I just want to end off by giving a huge appreciation to this hotel, the management, and everyone one of the staff. Thank you for the stay I wanted and was hoping for the day after my birthday.

My wife and I were recommended this place by a friend, and my wife figured we could swing by after a long day of driving and errands. We arrived at 8:30PM, saw the place was packed on walking in, and figured there would be a bit of a wait. My wife and I went to Domu to celebrate a birthday. Wish I had read the most recent reviews before coming here. Sad to say we didn’t have a great experience and the food was definitly disappointing. We ordered the shishito peppers, fingerling potatoes, chili cucumbers for appetizers and the Richie Rich and Spicy Tonkatsu ramen for mains in addition to 3 alcoholic beverages. Total came to $112. The peppers and the potatoes were good, but even then not great. Mostly it was the ramen that was disappointing. It lacked flavor, and several elements seemed to have been poorly prepared. We were one of the first groups in, but our ramen was room temp when we got it. As for atmosphere, if you have anxiety you may way to avoid. Seats are packed and several tables feel like you are sitting at the same table with people. It gets loud fast and you cannot hear each other mostly. The other thing we noticed is when you go to the bathroom, the walkway that is directly next to the kitchen and the farthest seats to the left has an AWFUL smell. It smells like pee or body order. Definitly not a fun smell at all. The service was nice and attentive which was why I didn’t give it a full 1 star. I am not sure if this was just an off night but we will definitely not be back.

Awesome place to dine. We came here after a celebratory event. We had a large group. Christian is an A+ server! And shout out to the whole staff, chefs, cleanup, everything is on point. We are always looking for places to stop for lunch when towing our camper, and this seemed like a great option. The satellite view showed a huge parking lot and plenty of outdoor seating, which made it look ideal for traveling with dogs. Unfortunately, we won't be back. A few things contributed to the experience: • Campers are not allowed in the main parking lot. This wasn't a major issue, but it was a Tuesday and the lot was mostly empty, so the rule felt a bit unnecessary given the size of the property. • Dogs are not allowed in the outdoor dining areas. We travel frequently with our dogs and have never encountered a restaurant with outdoor seating that didn't allow them. • Signs with various rules are posted throughout the property, including restrictions on outside beverages, dogs, and RV parking. We had no problem following the rules, but the amount of signage made the atmosphere feel less welcoming and detracted from the overall experience. • The food was good, but the pricing felt high for the overall experience. We ordered boneless wings and Boom Boom shrimp as appetizers, plus one beer and one glass of wine. No entrées or sides. The bill was $44 before tip and over $50 after tip, which felt expensive for what was intended to be a quick and convenient lunch stop. • The menu also included several restrictive notices. Individually, these wouldn't have bothered me, but combined with the numerous property rules, they reinforced the feeling that customer experience wasn't…

**The staff makes this place a 5-star experience!** Where do I even begin? Sometimes choosing a hotel is one massive headache. Do you focus on the quality, the location, or the service? While it’s all important, I don’t think anything tops fantastic service—and this team delivers. From the moment I checked in and severely embarrassed myself, I was rescued by Sebastian, one of the most kind and helpful valet employees I have ever met! Not only did he help me navigate a parking garage that I—for some reason—thought it made absolute sense to enter on the left side in America, but he was also such a pleasure to speak with every single day of my stay. Sebastian helped me get a shuttle over to the Kia Center for a concert (thank you, Fred! You were amazing!), and directed me toward our next A+ employee, Donna. Donna was a literal lifesaver when I checked in early, and she even helped me figure out the safest, most efficient way to get back to the hotel after a late night concert. I loved chatting with her daily... especially when it came to my terrible self-tanner streaks! While the rooms themselves are nothing to write home about—a bit older and nothing fancy—the staff is a solid five stars. Walking into a hotel where the team feels like a big family and genuinely cares about getting to know you is something really special. To the management team at the DoubleTree: Sebastian, Donna, and Fred deserve top-tier recognition! There were a few other employees who were absolutely…

Update: I have arranged and been promised a call from management 3 different times. No such call has ever occurred and they consistently ignore it. They do not care about guest satisfaction.
I loved everything, the room was clean and the beds were comfortable. The pool and the fitness studio were also great. I would definitely love to come back next time I visit Orlando

Every team member is amazing, friendly, and always willing to go the extra mile to make the stay comfortable. I would especially like to give a shout-out to Donna, who has been extremely customer-friendly and consistently wonderful over the past two years of my visits. Her kindness and professionalism really make a difference. I will definitely continue visiting this hotel and highly recommend it to others.

Walls are very thin and heard neighbors and people in the hall constantly. This hotel is definitely dated and in some SERIOUS need of renovations ASAP to be considered worthy of the Hilton name.

Unfortunately, those are the only good things I have to say about this place. Negatives: Room was dirty. It felt uncomfortable and unsafe, and there were small bugs crawling around everywhere. The room had a strong unpleasant smell, I couldn’t describe it. Elevator was TERRIFYING! Every time you got on it, it would shake, thud, and make loud noises. It felt unsafe. No hotel should ever be like this. There was no hot water, so I had to shower in cold water. I assumed there were bed bugs, so I wasn’t even gonna bother sleeping in that bed. Don’t know why this room was so dirty. This place needs to be cleaned entirely, because unfortunately some other people had the same problem as me. The health department needs to go here too. If they don’t, this place should just be shut down and instead replace this with another hotel. You should only recommend this place to your worst enemy. Save yourself the trouble and go somewhere else!

Positive: Location Negative: Was very disappointed in the hotel. Half of the lights didn't work, the toilet paper holder was broken and staff didn't fix after they said they would, the blowdryer was broken, there were stains on the drapes, there was mold in the air conditioner vent.

We were double charged and they refuse to make it right. We booked and fully paid for our reservation through Armed Forces Travel - a 3rd party through Priceline. The only anticipated cost should have been parking and the room hold fee. The day we checked in by a manager (who I think should have known better) they couldn't find our reservation, so rather than call Priceline to see where the disconnect was, the manager created a whole new reservation and charged us a higher room rate, the room hold fee, and parking fee - totaling 3x more than we originally paid Priceline. Did not disclose ANY of this to us. We noticed the charge a few days later. I called and explained the situation on 3/22, I was told to check my email for my refund, probably to get me off the phone to be honest. No refund ever came. We opened claims with both the banks the following week. Now almost a month later we receive a folio from DoubleTree of a $156 refund?? That's not even HALF????

Booked here to be close to Universal for our trip last week. Arrived and there is a BP gas station next door to the hotel, about three car lengths from the side entrance of the hotel. There is a homeless camp set up in the alcove of the gas station...complete with a mattress on it. It was around 6 PM at our arrival, and the people were coming in for the night by foot and off the Orlando city bus. Most of them appeared to be on something. We went in and looked at the room, which smelled very musty and was very dated. I told my family, "we are not staying here." I went down to the front desk and the person who was working, Samuel, was so friendly and helpful. I told him we were not going to be able to stay there. He asked no questions and got us transferred to the Drury Disney Springs. We had stayed at that Drury two years ago when we went to Disney. It is a night and day difference. Only put us 15 minutes from Universal. I had heard over the years about being in the Disney bubble, but never experienced the peace of mind it brought me until this trip. I have no doubt in my mind that my car would not have been there the next morning had we stayed at the Universal Drury. The hotel owners need to address this issue with the gas station IMMEDIATELY. They need to start by building a large fence between the hotel and the gas station. If I owned this hotel, I would be making some safety changes ASAP!!! I DO want to say that I cannot say enough good things about the front desk clerks.…

From a hotel stay perspective, this hotel was extremely clean, smelled great, and the service was very very good. The concierge and housekeeping displayed care and friendliness. Pros with this hotel are breakfast every morning and full breakfast not continental, 5:30pm snack time and drinks where the snacks were actually samplings of full meals. Free popcorn, and free coke product drinks starting at noon every day. Very impressive! Fitness center mainly focused on 3 treadmills and 2 ellipticals, and a set of free weights. If you’re looking for a basic workout, it will work, but nothing more. The pool seemed clean and somewhat safe, although the fence lent to a parking lot view to the pool which made it uncomfortable with the homeless population there. Plus, the pool was mostly in the shade. Now the cons, the location was unsavory to say the least. First off, this is not a location where you can walk to anything. There is a Drury hotel by Disney Springs, but don’t mistake this one for that one. You cannot walk to Disney Springs from this hotel. In fact, you can’t walk anywhere from this hotel, except to the 7-Eleven that’s practically in the parking lot and due to the eight lanes of traffic that a pedestrian has to get through to get anywhere, PLUS the homeless camp that was in the parking lot. Aside from the homeless camp it seemed to be a parking lot where most homeless and panhandlers just hung out all day. I wanted to go across the street to the Whole Food’s store, but…

We stayed here for one night before a cruise and were really disappointed. The photos are misleading — they make it look like an oceanfront property, but it’s not. Our room overlooked the parking lot, and there’s no real ocean view from most of the hotel. I travel frequently and have Marriott Gold status, so I’m very familiar with what to expect. When I asked for bottled water at check-in, I was told they “don’t participate in that,” which was surprising and not consistent with most Marriott properties. I was also told this hotel is independently owned, but regardless, it reflects poorly on the Marriott brand. We did eat at the pool bar, and I want to call out that the bartender/server was excellent — friendly, attentive, and clearly doing her best. The food overall was good, but my mahi was almost raw. When I sent it back, I was told they couldn’t remake it due to timing and was given chicken instead (which was cheaper), but the bill wasn’t adjusted. They offered a free dessert. Again, the server handled it well — this felt more like a management issue than a staff issue. Between the misleading photos, lack of basic elite benefits, and how issues were handled, I wouldn’t choose to stay here again — especially if you have Marriott status. I shared all this with the front desk clerk when I checked out, but there was no resolution with the restaurant charges.

We'd previously worked with Brittney on a much happier occasion (my dad's 80th birthday several years ago) and just knew that Dustin's BBQ was the perfect choice for his celebration of life. So, do ask for Brittney if you want the best for your catered event. She's a treasure! ⭐ The food was promptly delivered to the venue by Austin, a very professional and helpful young man. He arrived a few minutes early and made sure to set everything up and confirm the entire order with us before he left. He then asked if there was anything else he could do for us before he left the venue. Austin knew how important the occasion was to get right and it showed. He's a total pro! ✨ The food we chose was pulled pork, smoked chicken quarters (white and dark meat) and our sides were Hawaiian sweet rolls, green beans and macaroni and cheese. We also had ice cold gallons of tea and lemonade. They provided all serving spoons, eating utensils, plates, cups, lots of napkins, and even extra ice. The guests at my dad's celebration of life LOVED everything! I was most pleasantly surprised by the smoked chicken. It was SO flavorful without being dry. This is one of the best Mexican style restaurants that you will find with great specials during each week. On Tuesday, the authentic tacos are only $2.00 each. I suggest that you order at least three for your plate. These are high quality tacos that you will enjoy, especially the crunchy beef variety. Then on Wednesday, you can enjoy the fabulous beef Enchiladas served on a piping hot place and smothered with Mexican cheese. It's only $2.08 for each enchilada and I suggest you order 3 to be served on your really hot plate. Of course, a large basket of tortillas and a bowl of salsa is provided for no extra charge when you first place your order. The menu has such a great variety to choose from, so it's a little challenging to know what to select. Note, this is an old style restaurant with most of the employees speaking Spanish as their first language, but there is not a language barrier. These folks are hard workers and do their best to please their customers. Many of the locals come to this restaurant each week for the great food. If you ever get near The Villages, FL or Lady Lake, FL, you should definitely stop by and enjoy one of the best Mexican style restaurants in Florida. Best wishes!

The Wagyu beef dumplings were absolutely amazing and one of our favorite appetizers of the night. We also ordered the crab cakes and steak tartare, both of which were expertly prepared and full of flavor. I tried the Caesar salad as well—while it wasn't a traditional Caesar, it was unique, fresh, and very enjoyable. For our entrées, we enjoyed the rack of lamb, filet mignons, and a couple of lobsters. Every dish was cooked perfectly and delivered exactly the quality you'd hope for from a high-end steakhouse. The sides, including the mac and cheese, were equally impressive and complemented the meal perfectly. The true highlight of the evening was the Bananas Foster. It was absolutely phenomenal and easily one of the best desserts I've ever had. The presentation, flavor, and execution were flawless. From the exceptional food to the outstanding service, Eddie V's delivered on every level. A memorable dining experience that exceeded expectations, and we look forward to returning soon.

I recently stayed here as part of a dance nationals group and unfortunately my experience did not meet the expectations I have as a Hilton Honors member. The biggest issue was that after I called around 9:25 a.m. to request a late checkout, I later discovered my room key had been deactivated because I had not placed a personal credit card on file. I completely understand hotels requiring a card for incidentals, but at no point during check-in was I informed that my room would be locked if I didn’t provide one. Being locked out of my room without any warning was frustrating and embarrassing. While standing at the front desk, two employees openly discussed my situation in front of me. Having staff talk about a guest within earshot was unprofessional and made an already uncomfortable situation even worse. I do want to recognize the manager, Noah. He took the time to explain why the hotel has this policy, listened to my concerns, and genuinely tried to de-escalate the situation. Although I still disagree with the way the policy is handled, I appreciated his professionalism and willingness to help. He also refunded my daily parking charge after I questioned it. Speaking of parking, I was confused why I was charged each day when the parking gates were frequently left wide open. I watched multiple vehicles enter and exit without stopping, including people driving out through the entrance lane, so it wasn’t clear what the parking fee was actually paying for. Another disappointment…

The Enclave is a small apartment and was an AirBnb we rented near Universal for the first 15 days of our 21 days trip. It's made up of two rooms and a living room with a tiny kitchen and two seats at the bar. There is a small dining room table to eat at with four chairs. The kitchen is NOT made for a cook, but for travellers mainly eating prepared meals or meals out. Good for toasting bread or reheating leftovers mainly. There are a few staple appliances for breakfasts, but only one pairing knife (no other knives). The first night we killed 3 bugs (2 tiny cockroaches and a spider) and saw quite a few other dead bugs. We couldn’t find the broom and dustpan, so we just kind of lived with them, wondering how we were supposed to live here for 2 more weeks. But actually, keeping the front door closed and keeping the appliances, floors, and counters clean=very few bugs. We've seen one or two, description below, but overall the stay hasn't been terrible to this point. The air conditioner froze up before bed in night #1 and didn’t work well. The trick is to slowly lower the temp. The room is fairly cozy at 75°, but I wouldn't take it lower than 74°. There is no dresser in the main bedroom, but it’s in the living room, which is kind of inconvenient, but not terrible. The things that bother me the most–only having one tiny knife, no kitchen shears, no measuring spoons, and no kitchen linens. There is plenty of Raid and I see cockroach motels all over the room. There’s even a liquid…

Algumas coisas que você precisa entender primeiro: os apartamentos não são gerenciados pelo próprio hotel, cada um tem um dono, e esse dono subloca o apto, então cada apartamento pode ser bem diferente entre si. Sobre o hotel em si: localização ótima, fica perto do endless summer da universal, você consegue ir a pé (pouco mais de 5min de caminhada) e de lá pegar o ônibus gratuito do hotel para a universal. Fiz isso em todos os meus dias de universal e foi uma bela economia. Além disso, tem restaurantes e lojinhas por perto, tanto para ir a pé, quanto para ir de uber/carro. Tem piscina coberta e ao ar livre. Cada prédio tem apenas 4 máquinas de lavar e 4 de secar, não foi um problema quando eu fui mas dependendo do horário talvez você não ache uma máquina livre. Também não tem front desk 24h, mas em horários úteis tem uma front desk que recebe encomendas e tem pessoas caso você queira tirar uma dúvida. Sobre o quarto: o quarto específico que eu aluguei tinha um cheiro muito forte de umidade. Só melhorou depois de 1 semana lá (fiquei 2 semanas), e fiquei pensando se era porque meu host não deixava o ar condicionado ligado. O apto era espaçoso, tinha cozinha com microondas, fogão, todos os utensílios que precisava, e máquina de lavar, porém a cozinha tinha mini baratas que ficavam andando por lá, especialmente quando estava escuro. I normally do not write negative reviews, but I feel this experience needs to be shared so other families don’t go through the same situation. We booked a weekend stay at JS Luxury in Orlando through Expedia. The listing gave the impression that this worked like a regular hotel stay, but once we were already on the road (a four-hour drive), we began noticing that everything was handled digitally and that there was no front desk or on-site assistance. We paid the mandatory cleaning fee and completed everything that was required online. Immediately after that, our stay was cancelled. This happened while we were already driving to Orlando. We arrived around 10:30 PM, which was still before the stated midnight check-in cutoff, and tried to resolve the situation. Instead of trying to help us after such a long drive, the main concern we kept hearing was that Expedia had our money and not them. There was no flexibility, no real attempt to help us check in, and no clear communication about what could be done. What made the situation worse is that there is no real customer support. The phone number listed either went to voicemail or someone answered and hung up. Calling the Enclave reservation line also led to voicemail with no callback. At that point it was late at night, we were stuck in Orlando, and we had already paid close to $600. Because we had no guarantee we would get that money back. The entire trip was ruined, and it felt like the situation could have been handled much…

I have been a loyal customer of this restaurant for over six years and have always enjoyed the food, atmosphere, and value it provided. Unfortunately, the experience has changed significantly in recent months. Since Tony left in January, the atmosphere and overall management seem to have declined. The welcoming environment that kept customers coming back is no longer the same, and it shows in the overall dining experience. The only reason I will pass by is to see old friends (waiters and waitresses) that still remain faithfully working under these conditions. What is most concerning is the dramatic increase in prices. Many menu items have increased by more than 40%, making it difficult to justify dining here regularly. Paying close to $50 for an average plate of Cuban food feels excessive, especially when there are many excellent alternatives available. The wine pricing is equally difficult to understand—charging $78 for a bottle that can be purchased at local stores for around $11 feels unreasonable. I understand that restaurants face rising costs, but there is a point where pricing drives away loyal customers. After supporting this establishment for many years, I am disappointed to see the direction it is heading. Unless changes are made, I fear the restaurant will continue to lose longtime patrons and struggle to maintain the customer base that helped make it successful. I sincerely hope management takes customer feedback seriously and works to restore the quality, value,…

This was one of the most frustrating hotel arrival experiences I have ever had. We booked this hotel mainly because it was advertised as offering a free 24/7 airport shuttle. After a long flight, that was exactly the kind of service we needed. When we landed at Orlando International Airport, we called the hotel and the front desk instructed us to go to Terminal C, Ground Transportation level, pickup spot C271. We were told that the driver would be notified. So we rushed through the airport with our luggage because we did not want to keep the shuttle driver waiting. We went all the way to the instructed pickup point, waited there, and nobody came. When we called again, we were suddenly told that the shuttle service was no longer available and that we should take an Uber instead. So the hotel not only advertised a shuttle that apparently did not exist, but also sent us to a specific pickup point before telling us the service was unavailable. That is unacceptable. We had to walk around the airport unnecessarily with luggage, lose time, deal with confusion after a flight, and pay for Uber out of pocket. At the hotel, we were given an email address and told to send the Uber receipt for reimbursement. We sent two emails with the receipt and relevant information. No response. The room itself was acceptable, but that does not make up for the misleading shuttle information, poor communication, and complete lack of follow-up. If a hotel no longer offers a service, it should not be…

It's like Nona's hug was a smell...even without having a Nona...you're getting her hug here. Then the food. Get the meat wrapped in bacon. Get the lamb lollipops. Get the Salmon. Get a pasta. Get it all. You'll leave in a food coma but it's okay. You still smell like it so it isn't like you have to really say goodbye until you shower. The wine by the glass was too warm. That's my only inconsequential negative thought. I'd just stick to a beer next time or just a nice tea.

Absolutely fantastic experience from start to finish! The food was outstanding, the atmosphere was incredible, and the service was top-notch. If you’re visiting on a Saturday or Sunday (until they run out), the Lasagna is an absolute must. It’s only available those days, and it did not disappoint. The bruschetta was also fantastic and a perfect way to start the meal. The photos honestly don’t do the food justice — the lighting inside is low, but that’s part of what makes The Garlic such a unique experience. The ambiance is incredible, and the atmosphere is warm, inviting, and memorable. One of my favorite places in New Smyrna Beach to enjoy a great meal, especially when you’re craving something hearty and delicious. Can’t wait to come back!

Nothing tasted fresh. The only sides that were enjoyable were the coleslaw and beans, so 2 stars for getting the basics right. You have a choice of 3 BBQ sauces-and tiny they are-and you each DO NOT get 3 in your meal of 2. You also are given not butter exactly, but tiny packets of butter-flavored "whipped spread." As a parent, I expect reasonable communication, consistency, and respect when it comes to decisions involving my children. The manager's refusal to acknowledge my parental authority and his unwillingness to work toward a reasonable solution were both frustrating and unacceptable. If theater policy requires a parent to be physically present during a rated-R film, that policy should be enforced consistently at all times, not selectively depending on the day or the employee involved.The contradictory treatment my family received reflects poor customer service and a lack of clear policy enforcement. We spent our time and money expecting to enjoy an outing, only to be turned away…

Fig's Prime was my first visit, and it absolutely makes a strong first impression. Located in Altamonte Springs, the exterior is grand, parking is easy, and when I arrived there were multiple parties happening at once. It immediately felt like a serious date-night spot—also perfect for client dinners, birthdays, or celebratory gatherings. I went with a group of eight, and across the board, the steaks were the undeniable stars of the night. I got to admire a prime rib, filet mignon, and New York strip at the table—and every single one was cooked perfectly. I ordered the special: a 10 oz filet topped with three jumbo shrimp in a lobster cream sauce, served with mashed potatoes and asparagus. The filet itself? Perfect medium rare, exactly as requested. Seasoning was balanced and not overly salty (which is something I often run into elsewhere). The steak alone was excellent. The lobster cream sauce, however, was just okay for me. This is subjective, but I felt it leaned a little too creamy and slightly muted the savory depth of the steak. Personally, I would’ve preferred something brighter like a chimichurri—or if going the lobster route, perhaps a full lobster tail instead of shrimp to really justify the pairing. The shrimp were fine, but they felt like they were competing with what could have been. The asparagus was my only real food gripe—it was small and limp. Properly cooked, thicker asparagus can be vibrant green with a soft crunch. This missed that mark. We started with…

I visited Fratelli’s in downtown Orlando yesterday, and I have to say — the food was absolutely outstanding. Every dish we ordered was packed with flavor. The Fra Diavolo had the perfect kick, the Baked Ziti was rich and comforting, and the Penne with Bolognese (with added grilled chicken) was phenomenal. We also had a tomato, mozzarella, and basil salad, and it was incredibly fresh — the kind of simple dish that reminds you how good real ingredients can be. And I can’t forget the warm bread they served; you can tell it’s made fresh daily. The service was truly top-notch. Our server was attentive, fast, and friendly. Everything came out quickly, and the overall experience was solidly a 10/10. Fratelli’s just earned a spot on my list of Orlando favorites. Highly recommended.

Every dish I ordered was under $10 and sure, its the same 4 cheese tortellini you can get at hundreds of Italian restaurants across the country. But they know better than to put a $20 price tag on it. And the pizza is no better than any other small pie I've had. But I got to see the people behind the counter laughing, and enjoying their time at work. Who gets to say that about the service industry these days? They tried to steer me to their better dishes once they heard I was from Jersey. Fratelli's is a very special place, and if you can ignore the tacky Godfather music you'll learn to love it like they do. Very glad I got to come here.

My wife and I met another couple for lunch yesterday at First Watch on Sand Lake Road in Orlando, she explained to the server she had celiac disease and could eat no gluten. She ordered half of a gluten-free sandwich and salad. She became very sick with severe stomach pain, abdominal bloating and severe diarrhea within 30 minutes of leaving the restaurant. I returned and spoke with the manager who was courteous and professional and explained they do not have a gluten-free kitchen, but they do take precautions and someone checks each order before it leaves the kitchen for accuracy. The manager verified the server did indicate in her instructions to the kitchen that this was a gluten-free lunch entrée. I am writing this review a day after the experience, my wife is still very sick with severe symptoms. We understand the potential of cross contamination, but this degree of symptoms was likely much more than that. The most likely explanation is that she was served regular bread on her sandwich! I would be very careful as a celiac eating there, you need to verify everything with the person who brings out the food (who is not the server), so there is increased potential for mistakes.

Fresh Kitchen Lake Mary is a gluten-free foodie DREAM 🙌🌿 If you’re gluten-free and looking for a spot where you can actually relax and enjoy everything without stress, Fresh Kitchen in Lake Mary absolutely delivers. I love places where eating clean doesn’t mean sacrificing flavor, and this lunch was SO good. I built my bowl with cauliflower mash + sweet potato noodles as the base, added broccoli + chickpeas, and topped it with the almond-crusted baked chicken… every single bite was delicious. The flavors, textures, freshness—it all worked perfectly together. And let’s talk about that fresh beet juice… the perfect pairing. Crisp, refreshing, and such a great complement to the meal. As someone who actively seeks out gluten-free friendly dining spots, this is one of those places that makes life easy. A fully gluten-free kitchen is such a huge win for the celiac/gluten-sensitive community because cross contamination stress is completely off the table. Clean ingredients, fresh food, quick service, healthy comfort food, and options that actually taste amazing? Yes please. Gluten-free followers: this one is absolutely worth the stop if you’re in the Lake Mary area. 💕 📍 More gluten-free finds on Instagram: @glutenfreewithkeith #GlutenFreeApproved #LakeMaryEats

I took my daughter to Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar for her 28th birthday since neither of us had been before and she had heard good things. We drove from Palm Bay to Orlando to try it out. She ordered the pork chop, which had a very interesting flavor profile. I asked our server, Diana (who was absolutely wonderful—truly one of the highlights of the night, and we loved her heart-shaped glasses), if it had an Asian fusion seasoning because something about it tasted familiar to me as I’m half Vietnamese. She wasn’t sure at first but checked with the chef, who actually came out to our table to explain it. He said the pork chop was brined with cinnamon and ginger, which made total sense for the flavor I was picking up. It was really thoughtful of him to come speak with us, and he mentioned others had asked the same question and that it might be better clarified on the menu as a spiced brine. We appreciated the explanation. While it wasn’t bad, it just wasn’t what we expected, so it’s not something either of us would order again. The apples and glaze it came with were delicious, though. I ordered the ribeye medium, but it came out medium rare. I was okay with it since I can eat it that way, even though it’s not my preference. Diana immediately offered to have it cooked more, but I decided to leave it as is. My asparagus was good, but the chipotle mac and cheese was very bland and needed more seasoning. The potatoes au gratin also didn’t really stand out to us. Overall,…

As someone who’s very particular about pizza — especially coming from NYC — I have to say this place truly impressed me. The pizza was absolutely delicious and definitely one of the best I’ve had in the area. We ordered a Hawaiian pizza while the kids had pepperoni, and every slice was fresh, flavorful, and made with that authentic homemade touch. What stood out even more than the food was the hospitality. Although it’s a small spot, the owner personally came out to greet us when we arrived. When he realized it was our first time and that we were taking the pizza to go, he kindly suggested we stay and enjoy it fresh out of the oven. That level of care and attention instantly reminded me of the classic family-owned pizza shops back in Brooklyn. The service was exceptional from beginning to end. The staff brought us cups with ice for our drinks, extra parmesan, and all the seasonings without us even asking. Small details like that make a big difference and create such a welcoming experience. You can truly feel the passion, pride, and love that goes into both the food and the service here. Huge kudos to the owner and his amazing staff for creating such a warm and memorable experience. I highly recommend supporting this family-owned business — places like this deserve our support far more than the big pizza chains. The service here is great — staff are highly efficient. A cup of coffee is poured almost as soon as you sit down, and the food comes out quickly without ever feeling rushed. The coffee could be a touch stronger, but that’s more a personal preference since I’m used to a bolder brew. As for the food, the Million Dollar Bacon breakfast sandwich and the Summer Chipotle Steak Bowl were my favorites — both packed with flavor and very filling. One standout detail: the payment process. You can scan your receipt and pay directly from your phone, which frees up staff to keep focusing on other active tables. It’s a genius idea that keeps the whole experience running smoothly. My fiance, parents, and myself have enjoyed coming to First Watch for the past 2 years since I've discovered it. The ingredients are high quality and it's a more elevated breakfast experience for reasonable prices. Do not be turned away by the "multigrain" label, the pancakes are phenomenal and *massive*. One is usually enough to fill me up. I highly recommend ordering at least one thing from their seasonal menus before they swap them out. Most of the vegetarian options lean toward the sweet end and while tasty, sometimes that's too much sugar for me in the morning. Thankfully I've recently discovered that I can request for the meat to be substituted for other items. I usually substitute with black beans. I do NOT recommend doing this with the power breakfast bowl because I later learned from their website that the quinoa is cooked in chicken stock. That meal ended up being kinda bland anyway even when I added hot sauce. Also the quinoa in my opinion would be better if baked in the oven after boiling so there is more texture variety. My recommended dishes that I've had so far include: - chocolate chip OR lemon ricotta pancakes - avocado toast - AM super foods bowl - Barbacoa Chilaquiles Breakfast Bowl (swap beef with extra beans) - purple haze drink - mint mocha iced coffee drink My one critique is the first time I ate at First Watch I ordered a lavender french toast from one of their past seasonal menus and I have yet to see it again despite being almost two years. That was…

What our family likes about the Fun Spot is more than just the rides, which we like. It is the whole package. If we went to one of the major parks it would cost us a $grand$, not counting the additional fees for skipping or scheduling a ride on a major attraction. At those parks, For a thousand dollars we get the privilege of standing in one to two hour wait lines and at that rate you might get to ride six or eight rides. You would have to wade through crowds to get to anything. You know the drill, wasting your precious time waiting and standing in crowds. At the Fun Spot we can ride the same ride five or six times within the same hour, or hop from ride to another unencumbered by massive crowds. There are some very good roller coasters and rides, they may not have the big names like the major parks, but they still put a smile on our face and make the heart race. And, if you like go-carts they have a bunch of different tracks to pick from. Want to cool off, drop into the arcade area and play some games in a nice air conditioned space that serves cold drinks and snacks, and it will not break your budget. Best part is you can take four people here for the cost of one basic ticket at the major parks. Plus, if it gets too hot in the afternoon, take a break, go back to your condo chill until it cools off in the early evening and you still have five hours to ride until closing. Come and go as you want without walking four miles to do it, or having to hunt through an ocean of parked…

I spent a good five minutes looking at the menu because I just could not settle on one thing. I eventually picked the Eggs Benedict that came with a tomato salad - both of which were fantastic. I also opted for the non-alcoholic Royal Berry Spritzer. My table decided to share a Mickey Waffle. All of this left us full and satisfied to continue exploring the GF and other resorts! The prices are reasonable (especially for a WDW Deluxe Resort sit-down), and the service was fantastic. Cannot wait to visit again!

The menu had a good variety of brunch options that came out nicely prepared. The staff was very friendly and attentive! For $10 you get basically a fried shell with 2 quarter size pieces of lobster with overly battered meat. The batter was gooey and uncooked inside still and a complete disgusting mess. The lobster was inedible. I asked them about the lobster and they said thats how it was. I had to address them a second time and they tried to just ignore my request for refund. They took our info and said that corporate deals with refunds. This is not how we expected a Gordon Ramsay restaurant to be. I doubt we will see our refund and if thats the case I will submit all info I need to for our CC company to help handle this. This place isn't worth the hype, especially for how expensive it is.

Day two, still extending the St. Patrick’s Day theme, we had a burger with shaved corned beef, sauerkraut, cheese and secret sauce. Overall had a really good experience. We were impressed with the food at all the restaurants (minus old hickory just because we didn’t get to try). The hotel was huge, like it was its own city. We traveled with a 6 month old so we had plenty of areas so walk and things see. The saltwater pond was incredibly cool One thing was very disappointing though. The fridge in our room was at 56deg (brought thermometer) when we got there, it’s one of those fridges you have to hit the “2 hr cool” on, once you hit the 2 hr cool, it would get down in the 30s but then go back up. How is this safe for food? I went down to talk to the front desk and ask if they could do something about it because we had to keep breast milk in there, and they told me no, but you can bring your breast milk and put it the hotels fridge… That was completely unacceptable for so many reasons. So I had to go buy a cooler and keep filling it with ice. One area for improvement would be to change one of the two Starbucks to another coffee shop.

We ate at Wreckers twice is how good that buffalo cauliflower was! We also loved Theresa U. She provided great service and was really wonderful. Update: family trip late June 2026. As soon as I got to my room, I bumped into Annette H. from housekeeping and she’s an absolute gem. Her wonderful personality and urge to help others and say hello to my kids is what made this stay really stand out. I then went to the waterpark and the teens who are in charge are some of the most professional humans I’ve encountered. Some of the kids were absolutely harassing employees. We stood in line for a slide for about an hour due to an employee not showing up and kids were just hounding Brian and he really handled all of it so well and he was beyond patient and kind. Matthew who was another lifeguard manning the slides was awesome as well! They both were so nice to my kids over and over as they couldn’t get enough of the slides. Jeff at wreckers was very kind and funny and definitely enhanced our vibes at dinner. We were there at the busiest time possible and the hosts were handling everything so efficiently! The downside here is this place is severely understaffed and to add to it, they sell day passes so anyone can get into the waterpark for $50. If you cannot keep up with the guests who have rooms booked and paid a…

This stay completely changed my perspective on where to stay when visiting Nashville. This past weekend, I returned for the Alan Jackson concert, and all I can say is…wow. The hospitality started the moment I checked in with Joel. He is the definition of Marriott Brand Standards. As someone who stays in hotels throughout the year, it’s become rare to find a front desk associate who genuinely acknowledges your loyalty status and proactively offers the benefits you’re entitled to without you having to ask. That level of service seems to be a lost art these days, and Joel absolutely nailed it. Five stars to him alone. I also want to recognize Jason, who I believe was part of the concierge team. He was standing at the “How May I Assist?” sign and was incredibly attentive and welcoming. Mina at the front desk was equally wonderful, helping me with a late checkout and replacement room keys with a smile and genuine willingness to help. As for the hotel itself, I honestly had no idea just how much it had to offer until my last day. I found myself wishing I had explored sooner! 10/10 buffet that I stumbled upon looking for a last minute spot for breakfast!!!! The game room made me feel like a kid again, I wanted to play every game. The indoor water park looked amazing, and I immediately thought about bringing my nieces and nephews for a future trip because they would absolutely love it. Between the beautiful indoor gardens, shopping, restaurants, and even the complimentary shuttle to…

We had an amazing stay at Gaylord Palms! From the moment we arrived, the staff was welcoming, friendly, and attentive. The resort is absolutely beautiful, with stunning indoor gardens, water features, and immaculate grounds that make you feel like you're in a tropical paradise. Our room was clean, spacious, and very comfortable. There were so many things to do without even leaving the property, and the restaurants offered delicious food with great service. The attention to detail throughout the resort really made our stay feel special. Whether you're visiting for a family vacation, a couples getaway, or just a relaxing weekend, I highly recommend Gaylord Palms. We can't wait to come back!

Por supuesto. Aquí tienes una versión natural y apropiada para una reseña en inglés: I booked this hotel specifically to enjoy the pools, which were one of the main reasons I chose to stay here. Unfortunately, the pools were closed almost three hours before their scheduled closing time due to a supposed storm. The disappointing part is that it never rained, and the pools were never reopened. I completely understand that guest safety comes first during severe weather, but in this case the decision seemed unnecessary and significantly impacted my stay. If guests are paying to enjoy the hotel’s amenities, they should be able to use them during the advertised hours whenever conditions allow. Unfortunately, this experience did not meet my expectations.

Our family stayed during the homeschool convention to have our special needs daughter participate in prom and graduation. She was completely overwhelmed at the end and we left quickly, accidentally leaving her diploma under her chair. Within 30 minutes of leaving, I began a barrage of calls, had parents who were still there trying to find it, and received assurance after assurance that something as valuable as that wouldn’t be discarded. Todd S. An asst director finally reached out a week plus later and continued with what was now, fake assurances, including that he would call me, email me, etc. but did not. I totally get that it was us that left the item behind, but we gave specific information down to the chair where it was located, and called before they could have been breaking down the room. Given the level of importance of this item, there should have been something more than platitudes offered. In this day and age of instant communication, how hard is it to find the supervisor for the area in real time, send someone to search and ask relevant employees and maintain timely contact? I literally could have turned around and come back. My daughter is devastated. What is the most disturbing is the lack of concern and follow through. It’s unprofessional and not representative of the hotel brand. Unfortunately it has overshadowed every other aspect of our stay.
Amazing place!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Our stay at Gaylord Palms Resort was absolutely unforgettable! From the moment we checked in until the day we left, every detail exceeded our expectations. We stayed in a balcony room overlooking the breathtaking atrium, and waking up each morning to that incredible view made the experience even more special. The resort itself is stunning, immaculately maintained, and there is always something beautiful to see around every corner. The restaurants were top-notch, offering outstanding food and exceptional service no matter where we dined. Every meal felt like part of the vacation. The pool area was the highlight of our trip. Renting a private cabana was worth every penny—it came equipped with a safe, TV, comfortable sofas, and plenty of space to relax while still being just steps away from the action. It made spending the day poolside both luxurious and convenient. And the lazy river? Simply spectacular! It was the perfect way to unwind, soak up the Florida sunshine, and create unforgettable family memories together. Gaylord Palms is more than just a hotel—it’s a destination where memories are made. Whether you’re planning a family vacation, a couples getaway, or just looking for a resort that has it all, I can’t recommend it highly enough. We will absolutely be back!

Honestly, this was a really bad experience at Hot N Juicy on March 15. I had a very disappointing experience at Hot N Juicy on March 15. First, the mussels we ordered were clearly undercooked, and we even found an ice cube inside one of the shells. This is a serious food safety concern. While the staff replaced the dish after we reported it, this should not have happened in the first place. Second, when the bill arrived, the mussels were charged twice. This is unacceptable—if we hadn’t carefully reviewed the bill, we would have overpaid. Third, the staff apologized and said they had applied an additional discount for the inconvenience. However, after checking the final bill, they had only removed the duplicate charge—there was no actual discount applied. This was misleading and reflects poor communication. To make matters worse, I asked the restaurant to adjust the tip due to the overall experience. I was told a manager would call me back to resolve it. It has now been 5 days, and I have not received any follow-up. Overall, the combination of food safety issues, billing errors, misleading communication, and lack of follow-through made this a frustrating experience. This lack of accountability is extremely disappointing. It’s one thing to make mistakes, but failing to follow through on resolving them shows a disregard for customers.

Gringos Locos in downtown Orlando has been a staple for years, especially known for its creative tacos and the infamous Double D—which is basically Gringos’ take on a double-decker taco or a Taco Bell gordita crunch. It’s been a go-to late-night stop in the heart of downtown for a long time. That said, after visiting over the years, I can’t help but feel like the quality has slipped just enough to notice. It’s hard to put a finger on exactly why—maybe ingredient quality, maybe freshness—but something feels different even though the menu hasn’t changed much. When you’ve eaten somewhere consistently for years, those changes stand out. The queso is still a win. I usually order it alongside a couple of Double D’s, and it remains one of the highlights. The shells are still house-made and fried, which I appreciate, but the fillings themselves felt like they needed sauce to really come alive flavor-wise. One disappointment was seeing that the self-serve sauce station is gone—that used to be part of the charm and helped balance out some of the tacos. Losing that definitely takes away from the overall experience. All that said, I’ll still stop by from time to time. It’s open late, centrally located, and still scratches the itch when you’re downtown and hungry. It may not hit quite like it used to, but Gringos Locos still holds its place as a reliable late-night option in Orlando.

Se você procura um hotel econômico em Orlando, o Monreale Hotel é uma ótima opção. A localização é excelente, perto dos parques da Universal Orlando Resort e também dos outlets, o que facilita bastante a locomoção durante a viagem. O atendimento também foi muito cordial. Toda a equipe foi super atenciosa, mas gostaria de destacar especialmente a dona Sirlene, que foi uma querida: muito receptiva e nos recebeu extremamente bem. O hotel é bem simples, sem grandes luxos, mas atende bem à proposta de hospedagem econômica. Um ponto que poderia melhorar é a parte do chuveiro, que ainda tem banheira com cortina. Isso acaba sendo um pouco desconfortável, porque a água escorre facilmente para o piso do banheiro e molha bastante o ambiente. No geral, se a sua prioridade é economizar sem abrir mão de uma boa localização e de um atendimento acolhedor, o Monreale Hotel é uma ótima escolha.

Vou contar sobre a minha experiência: o Monreale Express Internacional Drive foi reformado e assim ele não possui carpete e os colchões são novos e extremamente confortáveis. É uma rede brasileira, e assim o conforto de ter atendentes que falam português é maravilhoso!!! Ele possui uma estrutura pequena mas que tem: piscina aquecida, Wi-Fi gratuito, lavanderia, estacionamento, ônibus gratuito para os parques, contudo, não utilizei o servo de transporte deles porque é uma opção com poucos horários e não é tão cedo. Assim, decidimos pegar Uber e saiu super barato os valores para os parques da Universal. Ah, quanto o café da manhã é opcional, com valores a parte mas se você preferir, pode comprar algumas coisinhas para armazenar no frigobar do quarto e fazer suas refeições no quarto mesmo, pois, é equipado com microondas e frigobar. A Localização é privilegiada, e eles possuem as melhores tarifas e excelente custo-benefício. Vejam meu vídeo que postei que você terá ideia de como tem coisas próximas (farmácia, restaurantes, hotéis da universal….) Os quartos não são barulhentos mas as portas ficam viradas para a rodovia. Para mim foi super tranquilo. O quarto é bastante amplo. Quando voltarmos, ele fará parte de um dos hotéis da minha viagem, com toda certeza.

Piscina com água suja e muito cloro, café da manhã fraquíssimo, café horrível, microondas piscando tela de led atrapalhando dormir , sendo necessário arrastar o móvel para tirar da tomada. Travesseiros ruins. Ar condicionado desliga
Muito vantajosa. Maravilhosa localização e custo benefício. Voltarei esse ano.

Minha experiência desde o primeiro momento foi muito agradável , fui recepcionado pela Sirlene que foi muito cortes comigo e com a minha família , me fez indicações de restaurantes próximos e me direcionou de forma assertiva com indicações na região . |Sem sombra de dúvidas eu indico o local e voltarei futuramente !
Gostaria de agradecer pelo excelente atendimento da Sra Sirlene da recepção. Muito atenciosa e carismática, além de falar português. Passei mal e ela prontamente me ajudou no meu idioma.
Excelente ubicación, limpieza y buen espacio para descansar

A equipe do Hotel Monreale foi muito prestativa desde os primeiros contatos, ainda no Brasil. Troquei e-mails em português sobre uma encomenda na internet que realizei e eles receberam, me informando o recebimento e fazendo a entrega no dia do check-in. Durante a estadia, havia micro-ondas no quarto, o quarto era confortável, havia café preto com e sem cafeína à disposição próximo à recepção durante o dia todo e a equipe foi muito dedicada em nos oferecer a melhor estadia, sempre com muita simpatia e, quando não falavam português, falavam espanhol. A proximidade com os hotéis da Universal (Endless Summer e Dockside), com o mercado Walgreens e com os parques da Universal também foi muito útil. Valor bastante atrativo, custo-benefício excelente! Recomendo!

Tivemos uma estadia muito boa no hotel. A localização foi excelente para a nossa viagem, principalmente porque estávamos naquela correria de parques, outlets e passeios o dia inteiro. Ter um lugar bem localizado, tudo muito limpo e o quarto bem espaçoso, fez muita diferença na nossa rotina.||O atendimento foi impecável!! Desde a recepção até as camareiras, todos foram muito educados e prestativos. Quero deixar um agradecimento especial ao José, que nos recebeu no check-in com muita educação, simpatia e uma energia maravilhosa. Esse primeiro contato já fez a gente se sentir bem acolhida.||Outro ponto que foi muito importante para nós foi o silêncio do hotel. Depois de dias longos andando sem parar, conseguir dormir bem fez toda a diferença para aproveitar melhor a viagem.||Dentro do hotel tem um quiosque da Royal Elite Tour, empresa da Diana, e isso nos passou bastante confiança. Decidimos de última hora realizar o sonho da minha mãe de ir para a Disney, e a Diana foi incrível do início ao fim. Ela nos orientou, teve paciência, foi muito atenciosa e fez parte de um momento muito especial para a nossa família.||No final, a combinação do hotel bem localizado, seguro, limpo, confortável, com preço justo, atendimento acolhedor, boas noites de sono e o suporte da Diana tornou nossa experiência ainda mais especial. Recomendo com muito carinho.

Tivemos uma boa experiência no hotel. O quarto é simples, mas funcional, e o fato de ter micro-ondas facilitou muito nossa estadia, principalmente para quem quer economizar ou fazer refeições rápidas. A localização é excelente, um dos grandes pontos positivos. Há várias opções bem próximas, como restaurantes brasileiros, McDonald's, KFC, mercados e outras conveniências, o que torna tudo muito prático. O atendimento também merece destaque, especialmente por contar com funcionários que falam português, o que ajuda bastante os brasileiros que visitam Orlando. Como ponto de atenção, a limpeza do quarto precisa ser solicitada. Na chegada, tivemos uma impressão inicial de que a roupa de cama poderia estar mais bem apresentada, embora não tenhamos tido problemas durante a hospedagem. No geral, considerando custo-benefício, localização e praticidade, ficamos satisfeitos com a estadia e voltaríamos a nos hospedar no hotel. Pontos positivos: ✔ Excelente localização ✔ Atendimento em português ✔ Micro-ondas no quarto ✔ Restaurantes e lojas próximas Ponto a melhorar: ✔ Limpeza e troca de enxoval poderiam ser mais evidentes e frequentes Recomendamos para quem busca praticidade e uma boa localização em Orlando.

Had lunch here with my kids and was pleasantly surprised by how many gluten-free options were available and clearly marked on the menu. I ordered the Pollo con Mole Verde tacos on corn tortillas, and my kids enjoyed a gluten-free quesadilla. The food was fresh, flavorful, and the habanero sauce brought the perfect amount of heat. The mole verde, fresh toppings, and house-made feel really stood out. What impressed me most was the service. I accidentally ordered an item that contained pork, and the team quickly corrected it without hesitation. They even let my kids keep the original item while remaking my order, which was greatly appreciated. The atmosphere is relaxed, the artwork around the restaurant is beautiful, and it’s a great spot for a quick lunch in Winter Park. While I have a few personal favorite Mexican restaurants in the area, I would absolutely come back here, especially when looking for gluten-free options 📍 More gluten-free finds on Instagram: @glutenfreewithkeith

Hard Rock Hotel Daytona Beach delivered a solid stay and generally lived up to expectations. The atmosphere is lively and fun, with live music, DJs, and easy beach access giving the property a true vacation vibe. Front desk, room service and store staff were exceptionally friendly and check-in was a breeze. My king suite was spacious and well-appointed, with nice touches like robes, a soaking tub, and a long balcony. The pool and hot tubs were excellent—open late and even featuring music piped underwater—and food and drink prices were surprisingly reasonable (for a resort). Their Constant Grind coffee shop was a couple bucks less than Starbucks and had decent quality offerings. That said, the hotel has its quirks. Parking was an absolute mess, with weekend valet charges climbing above $40 per night! ($25 to self park across the street). Some service was inconsistent, the pool bar remained closed, and access to Sessions Bar was oddly blocked by signage then locked during my stay. If you’re seeking a quiet beach escape, this isn’t the place, as the music and activity didn’t really wind down until close to midnight. Overall, I had a good experience and felt the hotel offered good value in the $100–250 per night range. While nothing about the stay truly wowed me, Hard Rock Daytona is a nice, energetic hotel that I’d happily recommend—though I’m not sure it’d be my automatic choice for future Daytona visits.

Overall, I had a good experience during my stay at the Hyatt Grand Cypress. The resort is beautiful, the location is convenient, and there are many amenities available to enjoy. The property has a relaxing atmosphere, and I especially enjoyed the dining options, including Four Flamingos, which was a highlight of my visit. There were a couple of areas that I feel could be improved. The parking situation was frustrating. I had a handicap parking permit, but the designated accessible parking spaces were frequently blocked by cones, which required me to get out of my vehicle multiple times to move them in order to park. Even after being moved to another parking area, I continued to experience the same issue with cones blocking the accessible spaces. This was inconvenient and made parking more difficult than it should have been. After bringing this concern to management several times they ultimately reimbursed me the parking fees. I just hope they fix the parking situation for those who have disabilities and should have quick and easy handicap access. I also visited the braid booth located near the pool area. I understand this is a third-party vendor and not directly operated by the resort; however, I was surprised that some of the services listed on their menu were not services the staff member was trained to provide. We’ve been returning for years, and every visit reminds us why we keep coming back. The property is exceptionally clean and beautifully maintained. The staff consistently provide outstanding service, demonstrating both professionalism and genuine friendliness that make every guest feel welcome. One of the things we love most is the incredible variety of activities available. Whether it’s riding bikes, paddle boarding, canoeing, paddle boating, or enjoying the scenic trails for jogging and biking, there’s always something fun to do. The pools are beautiful, the waterslide is a huge hit with the kids, and the nightly outdoor movies create wonderful family memories. The game room keeps the children entertained, and the fitness center is one of the best hotel gyms we’ve experienced, with everything needed to maintain your workout routine while away from home. The dining options are excellent, and we’ve always enjoyed the quality of the food throughout the resort. We also appreciate the convenience of room service and the ability to order special amenities and treats delivered to your room for celebrations and special occasions. One of our favorite features is booking a room that faces the theme parks. The views are fantastic, and being able to watch the fireworks from the surrounding parks each…

This happened for both room on different floors. Which means several maid are not doing their jobs. Desk staff also said they do not vacuum, only when they do deep cleaning when ever that is. Black mold in the bathrooms was horrible
Room was clean, plenty of pillows. Best part for us was the gluten free options on the breakfast bar!
Comfortable beds, good breakfast.

I have stayed at an abundance of hotels and this was not one of my pleasant stays. I am a Diamond Elite Member and Continuously tried to get an upgrade or move throughout my stay and finally the day before we check out they told me I could upgrade but I was moved to the same kind of room. And I continuously checked the website to make sure rooms were available and it showed plenty of rooms available. The first room I was in was right next to the pool so you could hear everyone outside at the pool and I couldn't open my blinds because then people could just see straight into my room. The vent fan in the bathroom didn't work and there was mold at the top of the shower. The door to the room was hard to open and even harder to close. When leaving for work one morning just after 6 AM I stopped to grab coffee And there was none, I was told that coffee would be put out when breakfast was put out.
