Don’t know how we didn’t know about this place! So happy we found it! It was a busy holiday weekend Father’s Day my husband and I were celebrating our first year anniversary of marriage. We didn’t even have to sit long. We walked in every table was packed. It was just moved to be. The food was amazing after sitting down. We did not have to wait long our servers greeted us with a smile. Recommended some items. Of course I went for it. Soon after receiving our plates, we realize my husband and myself could’ve just shared a breakfast. You get well over what you pay for and the food was hot when it came out fresh and I just love the homemade peach jam. The biscuits made from scratch everything was just so amazing.

Honestly the worst breakfast I have ever had. I got the meatloaf hash and it had 0 flavor. Asked for my eggs basted and they were overcooked. I tried to save the dish with some ketchup and it was still so horrible I couldn’t even swallow one bite. The fruit was either old or not ripe enough depending on which fruit you ate. I asked for chicken and waffles after instead since my dish was so horrible and waited over 30 minutes and no food had arrived. We made a reservation, which was smart because this place is POPPING. Big groups, small groups, HHaGG handled it all. We had a great server who explained every dish we talked about, ensuring we knew what we’d be getting. The serving size was insane, so you will definitely leave with leftovers or a crazy full tummy. I enjoyed every bite, and so did my table mates. We would definitely go back to try more items on the full but not insane menu.

Was staying on International Drive and kept walking past this place every day before finally going in on our last morning. Should've gone on day one. The sage fried chicken benedict was unlike anything I'd had at brunch before, massive, creative, ridiculous in the best way. Presentation alone is worth photographing before you eat it. The coffee stayed full the whole meal without asking. Loud inside on a weekend morning but the energy is fun and nobody seemed to mind. If you're in the area and skipping this place, reconsider.

Huge portions of traditional farm fare like pancakes, french toast, biscuits, and fried chicken. Come hungry and leave with your next meal. Located right off I Drive by Universal Orlando, it’s convenient if you have a car when you’re in the area. Plenty of tables for large parties. The food here is over rated. The price was good and the service was ok. They messed up a couple of people's orders in our group but the waiter made it right for one person.

We had a reservation and waited over an hour past our reservation time and still weren't seated so we ended up leaving like many people did. I understand it's a busy weekend and if we had just walked in I'd get it. But waiting over and hour past your reservation time when you showed up on time just seems like poor management to me.

Our waitress was nice and attentive, unfortunately the food left a lot to be desired. The coffee was loaded with sugar but very little actually caffeine content, the fathers day pancakes were good the hash browns were barely cooked. I asked for them to be crispy. The waitress went back to the kitchen to inform them and they came out with another plate about 10 minutes later (I was pretty much full at that point) that looks exactly the same as the first and the man said "crispy potatoes" as he dropped them off as if that somehow made them not exactly the same. My wife's French toast was good but the eggs she said tasted powdered. This is the second location we've been to. The first one was much better food wise. What an incredible experience at the Hangar Bar in Disney Springs! From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere transported us straight into an Indiana Jones adventure. The attention to detail is remarkable—the props feel authentic, the décor is immersive, and every corner tells a story. Whether you’re a Disney fan, an Indiana Jones fan, or just someone who appreciates great themed experiences, this place is a must-visit. The highlight of our visit was our server, Becca. She was absolutely exceptional. Not only was she friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable, but she took the time to explain the history and backstory behind Indiana Jones and many of the artifacts and details throughout the restaurant. Her enthusiasm was contagious and elevated our entire experience from a simple meal to a memorable adventure. Outstanding customer service is what separates good restaurants from great ones, and Becca exemplifies Disney-quality hospitality at its finest. Combined with the fantastic ambiance and immersive theming, this was easily one of our favorite stops at Disney Springs. A huge thank you to Becca and the entire team for making our visit so special. We’ll definitely be back!

It must be genuinely difficult to be a Universal executive and spend your entire career being compared to Disney. You have my sympathy. Mostly. The Wizarding World of Harry Potter is remarkable. Walking into Hogsmeade for the first time does something to you that you don't entirely expect. The Leaky Cauldron is atmospheric, the food is decent, and the butterbeer is worth the hype. They've built something special. And then your shepherd's pie arrives on a styrofoam plate with a plastic fork. I visited Disneyland last year. The food — which nobody goes to a theme park expecting to write home about — arrived on real plates, with real cutlery, like they'd considered the possibility that eating is part of the experience. It was a small thing that turned out not to be small at all. Universal has conjured an entire magical world. They've reproduced Diagon Alley brick by brick. Somewhere, someone spent months perfecting the exact shade of butterbeer foam. And then, apparently, the meeting ended before anyone got to the part about whether a plastic spork was the right vessel for delivering this experience. You're in a world of wizards. You can do better than styrofoam.

Breakfast daily at Fuel was convenient and better quality than Disney resorts. They even have Mickey waffles! Loved the chocolate malt from the Fountain. Loved being on the boardwalk. Boat transportation was great. Busses were good. Educate yourself to avoid frustration. For example, the Disney Springs bus drops off and picks up on the opposite end of Disney Springs then where the Disney busses are. Parks on the monorail lines... busses come and go from the Transportation and Ticket Center so you have to monorail in. It's fine. Just be aware. I didn't love not being able to just tap and go with my magic band for purchases but it was a minor inconvenience. Pool was great, too. Seats filled fast by late morning but there are multiple pools lots if chairs. Ordering food delivered right to your lounge chair was awesome and to pool food was really good... buffalo chicken flatbread! Lastly... EPCOT fireworks from our balcony! Great stay!

This is mostly a shout out to Christian who works at Lagerheads while he's pursuing a career in law enforcement: Me and two of my friends were headed to Flagler Beach on our bikes. One of my friends dumped his bike hard just north of Lagerheads. I went into the restaurant to ask for some napkins because there was some heavy bleeding. Christian and another staff member handed me a handful of paper towels and then Christian looked out the window at my bleeding friend and grabbed the first aid kit, put on some gloves and came outside to help stop the bleeding. With the paper towels and a butterfly bandage we managed to slightly close the wound and stop the bleeding. Then Christian gets us a bag of ice to help with the swelling. My friend ended up in the ER where he got an MRI and 9 stitches. But the staff at Lagerheads has to be commended. They could have just given us napkins and wished us luck. Fortunately, they employ people like Christian and the young lady (whose name I didn't get but she was awesome too) that genuinely care about people. We will be back soon to enjoy the food and I'm sure what's to be some great customer service. Thanks Lagerheads and Christian!

IF you’re looking for an amazing breakfast at Disney World, Kona Café at Disney’s Polynesian Village Resort is absolutely worth the reservation. The food here truly stands out and feels like a little Hawaiian escape right in Florida. We ordered the macadamia pancakes, and they were honestly something special — fluffy, rich, and different from your typical breakfast pancakes. They really gave that tropical Hawaii vibe. The loco moco was delicious and tasted incredibly authentic. But the absolute standout was the Samoan Benedict. We haven’t seen this dish at other Hawaiian restaurants before, and it was unique, flavorful, and an absolute must-try. The service was perfect from start to finish. The staff were friendly, welcoming, and genuinely seemed happy to be there, which made the experience even better. Food came out quickly, and everything was fresh and beautifully prepared. The restaurant itself was very clean, and the chairs were surprisingly comfortable. It’s not an intimate or quiet atmosphere — it can get a little loud — but honestly, the food more than makes up for it. Definitely make a reservation because this place is popular for good reason. Kona Café ended up being one of our favorite breakfasts at Disney World!

It was our first time dining here. The Poly is a beautiful resort. We went for breakfast and only waited 10 minutes to be seated, but it seemed like it took an eternity to get our food. It was 1 hour and 10 minutes from check in until we signed the bill. I’m not sure if that’s normal or not, but we really like our waitress and didn’t have any other plans for the day so the wait wasn’t an issue. The Tonga Toast was thick….like thiccc but the syrup and cold strawberry compote soaked right in. I enjoyed it and I liked the strawberry with the warm banana center. It also came with a pile of bacon. I don’t mean 1-2 sad little floppy pieces, but a mini stack of crispy bacon which is my favorite breakfast meat! The ham and cheese omelet was really good too! We actually liked it just as much as the Tonga toast. The grits were perfectly cheesy. Not too runny and not too thick. Just right and we cleaned that bowl! Overall it was a wonderful experience and we’re looking forward to going back.

Food so good I forgot to take a picture of it. My dad and I both agreed the duck fried rice was absolutely stunning. The glaze on the duck leg is something very similar to a hoisin sauce, and it was cooked to absolute perfection. The rice itself was great, with these cucumbers that had a nice taste and crunch and some peppers for a great, surprising spicy note. My mother had the steak, and said it was wonderful. I had a small piece of it, and it was certainly a great taste. I'd recommend the duck over the steak though, there's many places in the resort for great steak! Desserts were impeccable; the little cookie on the cream tasted like a burnt samoa and that's a flavor I never knew I needed! The drinks were also great. I had the non-alcoholic orange specialty, it tasted just like an orange dreamsicle. Only small service hiccup was when checking in for our reservation, the CM didn't actually check us in so we sat for 15 minutes past our reservation time before we noticed on the app we weren't checked in. When we brought it up, another CM promptly fixed it. No worries there! Overall, HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Great use of a table service credit if you're on the DDP by the way; $45-55 a person meal/soda only before upgrades.

A new favorite place to eat while in Magic Kingdom! We're gluten-free and were amazed that we could eat just about anything on the menu. The Pao de Queijo (cheesy bread bites) were amazing. Kelly (from Ohio!) is an awesome waitress. We're thankful for her outstanding service.

I see why Skipper Canteen has one of the lowest ratings on Google for Magic Kingdom. The service is slow, the food portions are small and rather expensive. This restaurant used to be really good and a great value, it’s gone down in quality a lot over the years. Won’t be back, which is sad.

At first, the place appeared to be neat and clean, but after we ate, while waiting for our bill, a child dropped his drink on the floor. Later, the server cleaned it up using the same napkins people use to wipe their mouths. I immediately felt disgusted as they stepped on them and used them like a mop. For a nice restaurant, they should at least use a mop or a different type of cloth to clean the floor—not the same napkins people use to wipe their mouths. I was disappointed to see that.

We were pleasantly surprised with our meals. This is the probably the first time in my 40 years coming to MK that I had a sit down meal with a server. Atmosphere was pleasant and service was friendly. I was so excited to have my first alcoholic beverage at MK and the Sunset margarita was good. It could have been stronger, but it was very satisfying on this 90+ degree day The server did tell me it was premade. Now for the food ! We started with the Brazilian Cheese Bread with Chimichurri off the “secret” menu and it was so good! We also split the Jungle Green Salad and Hangar Steak. The salad was decent but could’ve used more dressing and the hanger steak was absolutely delicious! It was cooked a perfect medium rare and was so flavorful and tender. My son got the Cola-Braised Barbecue Beef off the kids menu and it was also very tender and had a great flavor! He also got the Enchanted Orange Dream non-alcoholic drink and it was so yummy! I don’t usually leave a lot of reviews, but I’m a foodie who was pleasantly surprised and wanted to share! Sorry, I was so excited to eat and drink that I forgot to take pictures!

Restaurant version of the Jungle Cruise. Great fun, great atmosphere, hokey "dad" jokes, great service, great food. Period. I've eaten here four times already and each meal was better than the previous one, the last one being the duck fried rice - it was AMAZING! I love how immersive the experience was too! Don't forget to order the pao di quiejo - too delicious to pass up! One word of caution - this locale is for the adventurous eater, but unique nonetheless.

​There is so much to love about this restaurant. It’s a truly immersive experience, transporting you to the off-duty mess hall for the skippers of the Jungle Cruise, which also happens to double as a secret meeting hall for S.E.A. ​As one of the few places to grab a cocktail in the Magic Kingdom, it’s worth a visit for the drinks alone (which are fantastic), but the food is the real surprise. The menu is an impressive blend of Asian, Latin, and African flavors that punch way above "theme park" standards. Plus, thanks to the Jungle Cruise connection, the servers deliver top-notch puns too. ​For all these reasons, I think this is easily the best restaurant in Magic Kingdom and a top-tier contender for all of Walt Disney World.

We visited The Juicy Crab tonight and were disappointed with the service. The staff were not particularly friendly, and we were asked if we wanted our bill before we had even finished our meal, which made us feel rushed. The most concerning part of the evening happened after we paid and left the restaurant. Our waiter followed us outside and asked to speak with my partner. He then told us that we needed to pay a $20 tip, explaining that it was mandatory because the staff do not receive basic pay and rely on tips. There was no mandatory gratuity listed on our bill, so this came as a surprise and made us feel very uncomfortable. We understand that tipping is customary in the USA and are happy to reward good service, but we do not believe customers should be pressured into leaving a specific amount. Unfortunately, this experience spoiled what should have been an enjoyable meal.

The next day, housekeeping knocked on my door around 2 PM asking why I hadn’t checked out yet. Absolutely incredible experience from start to finish! This is easily one of the best kosher schnitzel in Orlando area! The schnitzel itself is the star—the breading is perfectly seasoned and stayed incredibly crispy while the chicken remained moist and tender on the inside. I highly recommend getting it in a fresh, warm baguette; the texture combination is just perfect. What really sets them apart is the variety. Their selection of sauces and fresh toppings allows you to completely customize your meal.

During our visit to Orlando, trying out all their dishes was definitely a highlight of our trip. They have very generous portions with the entrees big enough to share. The best shnitzel I've ever had, even if you're not a chicken lover, you will fall in love. Crunchy and chewy, yet moist and fresh. The ribeye Steak was an underrated dish, delicious just like in a fancy steakhouse, cooked to perfection. The burgers were also out of this world, paired with the best fries I've ever had. The ground beef Kebab was also finger licking good! So moist and flavorful. The sides were marvelous as well: lemony white cabbage, creamy purple cabbage, savory rice and beans, fresh Israeli salad and even the onion rings with their garlic mayo sauce were a winner. We also enjoyed their Shabbat takeout food, absolutely yummy. You can taste the fresh ingredients. The Moroccan fish, beef cigars, babaganoush, humus AND THE MAKLUBA. OMG! The Makluba has to be one of the most innovative dishes I've ever had. A blend of ingredients (mushrooms, pesto, onions and shnitzel) with basmati rice cooked to perfection. Next time you go to Kosher Grill you have to try the MAKLUBA.

The Lakeside Inn is one of those places where you have to appreciate it for what it is. Walking through the doors felt like stepping into my grandmother's house, in a nostalgic, historic kind of way. Considering the hotel dates back to the late 1880s, it's impressive how well it's been preserved over the years. The staff was genuinely friendly and welcoming, and our room was clean, with a neatly made bed and fresh towels waiting for us. The location right on the lake is beautiful and is undoubtedly the hotel's biggest asset (sunset was amazing!). That said, the property is showing its age in some areas. There are quite a few small maintenance items that could be addressed, including fresh paint in places, very dirty windows, and worn carpeting that appears to date back to maybe an 80s or 90s renovation. I understand that being directly on the waterfront creates extra maintenance challenges, but a little attention to detail would go a long way. My room was quite small—honestly, my camper bedroom is larger—but it was functional. I would have preferred a small desk instead of a chest of drawers, especially since it was topped with four water cups despite the room realistically could never accommodate four people. The bathroom faucet leaked continuously no matter how tightly it was turned off, and the room only had blinds, so quite a bit of night light came through. The pool was surprisingly warm (my watch read about 92°), which made it less refreshing on a hot Florida day, and…

Beautiful old place in an excellent location. Lake views are spectacular and the front desk is attentive and professional. Took off a star because there was an overall "rickity-ness" to the facility that couldn't be overlooked. Sunken floor sections, difficult doors, slow hot water... Lack of outlets for charging tech...All can be explained by the hotel's age, but we've stayed at older places and they've addressed these matters. If 4.5 stars was possible, that'd be my hit. Nothing is a "deal breaker". If I'm ever in the area, I will DEFINITELY stay here...

Sort of funny how the wife and I found this place. I started this system when there were no smart phones, and continue this method even as they exist. If in a town and wondering where I should go, I seek out a bar with an adjective-animal in its name. Blind Pig. Fainting Goat. Happy Monkey. Whatever. Yes, I know a mermaid is only half fish, but it is my game and therefore it qualifies. Anyway, another thing my wife and I seek out is FONDUE. Thus, when we crossed my search of adjective-animal bars and her search of fondue...bingo. We made a great choice. This place just bleeds good vibes from the moment you walk in. Unique exterior, beer garden area, cool wall decor, corners with all sorts of stuff going on, cool outdoor patio area, and, most importantly, great service. Thor (I assume one of the managers) greeted us, and elevated our experience. He was just covering until the other bartender came on, but we enjoyed the heck out his friendliness, efficiency, humor, and knowledge of the menu and of the bar. We got the three cheese fondue dish, and it was amazing. Plenty of cheese, plenty of dippers. We didn't add protein (I believe that cheese has protein in it), and I thought the pretzel and potato were the best dippers, although bread is a given as a good choice. PLENTY of beer on tap, and I had the Dogfish Head 90 Minute IPA. Wife had the rose and liked it also. We went when they first opened, but you just had a feeling, looking around, that the place got FUN later on.…

JW Marriott Bonnet Creek strikes a fantastic balance between luxury and value. While it may not reach the level of a Ritz-Carlton or Four Seasons, it also comes with a more approachable price tag. Check-in was smooth, the staff were exceptional, and the location is hard to beat for Disney Springs, the parks, and the water parks. The room was clean, comfortable, and thoughtfully appointed, featuring robes, Epsom salt, quality bath products, ambient lighting, and an Illy coffee machine. The spacious bathroom and incredibly comfortable bed were highlights, though ceramic coffee cups, wine glasses, and a rainfall showerhead would have added an extra touch of luxury at this price point. Service truly stole the show. The staff even called to let us know when the pool reopened after bad weather, a thoughtful gesture that went above and beyond. The pool area was a lot of fun, although the pool bar closed earlier than expected. The biggest drawbacks were the hefty $55 resort fee and the underwhelming food quality at JW Market, despite the warm and friendly staff. I’ve had better breakfast sandwiches at Wawa for 1/3 of the price! Also, you have to go to the 12th floor for ice, which is an inconvenience. Overall, JW Marriott Bonnet Creek exceeded expectations and delivers a wonderful sweet spot between a standard four-star hotel and true luxury. If you’re willing to spend a little extra, especially when using points, I highly recommend it. Will definitely be back!

Personas como María hacen la diferencia y reflejan una verdadera vocación de servicio. Estamos muy agradecidos por su hospitalidad y sin duda la recordaremos con mucho cariño. ¡Gracias, María!

The most serious issue occurred when a bellboy pushing a heavily loaded luggage trolley struck me forcefully in the back while I was waiting outside the lobby. The injury caused significant pain and affected the remainder of my family holiday, including our first Disney trip. I was unable to enjoy attractions, struggled to walk for extended periods, and could not fully use Disney tickets and services that had already been purchased. What made the situation worse was the hotel's response. After reporting the incident, I experienced repeated delays, poor communication, and a complete lack of management involvement. I had to chase updates multiple times, received little meaningful follow-up, and was repeatedly referred to Security rather than being contacted directly by a manager. Apart from one compassionate engineer who offered assistance after seeing me struggling, nobody appeared genuinely concerned about my wellbeing. Throughout the entire process, I felt ignored, dismissed, and unsupported. A simple call from management, medical assistance, or any gesture of…

I’ve been here a few times with my family, we always have a great time. The spring itself is beautiful and cool, the “lazy river” is great, there’s hiking trails and a basic concession stand. A few things you may want to note before going, the springs open at 8, I got there at 8:05 on a Monday and the line was probably half a mile long already. It’s pretty busy no matter the day of week in the summer. You can bring your own tubes. Only half of the bathrooms are open in the morning unless it’s a busy day. And some of the doors in the ladies bathroom don’t close the whole way which is obviously a bit dangerous. There’s lots of rocks, I’d bring water shoes. If lightning is within ten miles (I believe) everyone has to be out of the springs for 45 mins. Take your own food but do not leave trash. Be mindful of other people. DO NOT TOUCH THE WILDLIFE! There are turtles, otters, fish, alligators, lizards etc everywhere that have this spring as their home, the amount of people I saw putting baby turtles in buckets and just leaving them on the side of the spring was honestly sad. Their lifeguards are great, while they’re young, every one I spoke to was helpful and cared about the safety of not only the people but the animals as well. With this being said, if you tell a lifeguard that someone put an animal in a bucket and tell them who, they will take the bucket take it to an area with less/no people.

My family and I had a great time at Kelly Park. It is an excellent destination for a family vacation, especially during the summer. The natural spring is beautiful, the water is crystal clear, and the lazy river tubing experience is fun for both kids and adults. One important thing to know is that the park fills up very quickly, especially on weekends, holidays, and during summer vacation. If you plan to visit, make sure you arrive early. I recommend being at the gate before 7:00 AM. We arrived early and had no problems getting in. However, if you arrive around 8:00 AM or later, there is a good chance the park will reach capacity. In that case, staff may give you a return pass or parking ticket and ask you to come back later, sometimes around 1:00 PM, when spaces become available. To avoid disappointment and make the most of your day, arrive before 7:00 AM, bring your tubes, sunscreen, snacks, and be prepared for a full day of fun. Overall, Kelly Park is a beautiful place for swimming, tubing, picnicking, and enjoying nature with family and friends. I highly recommend visiting, but getting there early is the key to a great experience.

The only thing that could be improved is the attitude of the hosts at the main entrance, as they seemed a bit cold. But honestly, even that somehow felt very French and part of the experience. Overall, we really enjoyed our visit and would definitely come back.
If I'm honest, it was way too heavy and mediocre in flavors. Easily the worst meal of our trip and way too expensive for what you get. Look elsewhere in World Showcase.

I’ve been to Epcot many times and always wanted to dine at Chefde France. I was treated to my first visit last weekend. The atmosphere and environment was absolutely lovely. Our server , Marlene, was magnificent and made the dining experience truly enjoyable. She helped us with the menu and made some modifications so that we got the best deal possible. The bread was fresh and delicious. I will say, the Cordon Bleu and the ratatouille were only very average. Not exactly the culinary experience I was expecting, but Marlene and the restaurant atmosphere make me want to dine there again.
We Go to the actual country of France often. This is solid brasserie level experience even for France , in Disney . Staff good - package meal fairly priced. 5/5. Interior nice energy.

Convenient for sea world but 30 mins to universal or Disney. Otherwise it’s a great hotel with solid restaurant options. Drive out of resort and there are a lot of local restaurants to go to too. It was rather busy the weekend before July 4th. 30-45 minutes for a slide! That wait stunk!

I wish I could give this resort more than 5 stars! We had an incredible experience from the beginning to the end of our stay. Our check in was smooth and accommodating, our room was extremely clean, and plenty of luxury amenities. Customer service is top notch throughout! The pool area is extensive and the kids loved the water slides! We ate at several restaurants including dinner at the Ritz. Our favorite places to eat were Cafe bodega for a quick breakfast and delicious coffee and the knife and burger near the pool. The cuban sandwich and burgers are so good! Chair side service at the pool was limited but everyone was so friendly. The fireworks were beyond incredible and a big highlight! I highly recommend staying here and booking a balcony room with a pool view. We can’t wait to visit again soon! Thank you for making our stay so memorable!

Primo is not really for hotel guests. , citron more for convention folk, the farm to kitchen definitely not for 5yo, how about an ice cream shoppe ? How about a food friendly kid place? Room service will kill the budget. They need work on this

I had been to presentations with my parents growing up, so I vaguely understood the process and had considerations on purchasing a package for my growing family. I was surprised that they did not provide food, like the presentations I attended with family growing up. Days before the scheduled presentation, we considered an additional day at the property we were booked at, as it was very nice. Communication was seamless with the Cypress Harbor staff. I was disappointed in the vacation club staff and their lack of communication with the resort staff to add the additional day. The request was never generated and sent to the resort by the rep I spoke with. Upon following up, the front desk had nothing on record. Additionally, the resort attempted multiple forms of contact to the vacation club on my behalf and they failed to return communication via voicemail and/or email to front desk management. During the presentation, I was pleasantly disappointed in the lack of professionalism by both the sales presenter and manager. It was filled with rhetorical questions, condescending remarks and very pushy to apply for a credit card and instructions on how I need to use my points. When I was asked if I had any questions throughout the presentation, I was interrupted each time I asked a question, so I…

I joined some friends for a casual bowling night at Kings, and I felt compelled to leave a review because of the exceptional service we received from the Hospitality Manager, Michael Osteen. What impressed me most was that we didn't ask for any special accommodations, but Michael was incredibly observant and proactive. My friend’s daughter has special needs that require a bit more sensory consideration, and Michael noticed this immediately. Without us even requesting it, he moved our group to a smaller, more private room where she could feel more comfortable and at ease. He also went out of his way to gift her a multi-color light-up toy. It was such a thoughtful, kind gesture—she loves sensory lights, and it kept her happy and engaged the entire night. Seeing a manager take that kind of initiative to ensure every guest feels welcome and included was a true 'hospitality moment.' Michael’s kindness made a huge impact on our evening, and it’s clear he genuinely cares about the experience of every person who walks through the door. Highly recommend!

We come to Orlando 3, 4 times a year and we come by Landry's often. The food didn't measure up to the service we got from Jackie, who was great and on point. My wife and I shared an entree along with 3 appetizers. Specifically, we paid $22 for ½ dozen chargrilled oysters. $10 would be too much because they were too too small. It should also state on the menu that there are only 6 oysters in that appetizer. The clam chowder was lukewarm. The Southern Fried Fish came out hot and was good as long as you was eating it. Trying to engage it after 5 minutes and the breader would separate from the fish. The absolute worse was the shrimp and crab cake. The execution in making this was acceptable. Once I worked into it it became loose and runny. Binding of the ingredients didn't happen and that was too bad. Too much happened and sending it back wasn't an option because between the bar and the seating area there were 3 active tables in the restaurant and no reason for food to come out cool, undercooked. I boxed up the majority of what was left only to get to my Airbnb and trash it there immediately after getting to my place. Moving forward this place will no longer be my go to spot for a meal. Ticket was $90 charged + $20 cash tip.

This place is a gem! Danielle was our server, and she was incredibly attentive throughout our visit. Honestly, all of the staff were super attentive and made the experience even better. Overall, the food was delicious! The only thing that didn’t fully convince me were the oysters — as someone who eats oysters often, they seemed a bit too small to be Virginia oysters, at least in my opinion. Besides that, everything was amazing! They have a great lunch deal, and the clam chowder was absolutely delicious, just like the calamari. The drinks were really tasty and beautifully presented as well. This is officially my new favorite seafood spot in Orlando! It’s definitely a must-visit if you’re in town. They also offer plenty of non-seafood options, which is great, and the prices are very reasonable compared to other places.

We tried liberty tree tavern for the first time after many visits to Magic Kingdom, and it was by far my favorite restaurant we ate at the whole week!! The all you can eat, family style, is an amazing switch up from the regular WDW restaurant styles. The food was amazing, 10/10. My favorites were the ham with the delicious apple glaze, the housemade cranberry sauce, and the stuffing. The dessert was outstanding as well. I wish I had a bigger stomach!!!! The atmosphere was amazing for an America lover, and the colonial theming was fantastic. We sat in the George Washington room. The restaurant can be loud with the large families coming in, but the service and theming made up for that.

The ultimate Magic Kingdom "Reset Button"—A Must-Have Reservation! Liberty Tree Tavern should honestly be 6 stars—don’t change a thing! This is a must-have reservation for any long day in the Magic Kingdom. The fresh, wholesome, home-cooked food is exactly what you need to fight the "theme park fatigue" that sets in after hours of walking. The Patriot’s Platter is filling and delicious, making it feel like a real meal that fuels you up to tackle the rest of a chaotic day with the kids. It’s comforting, reliable, and feels like home in the middle of all the park energy. If you need a break that actually leaves you feeling satisfied and ready for the fireworks, this is the spot!

I believe if they cut back on salt, sugar, chemicals the food would be more enjoyable. All in all we a nice experience.

Pro tip; this fantastic restaurant and the Diamond Horseshoe restaurant share a kitchen. While the Horseshoe's menu has varied in the past, now it is exactly the same fantastic meals you get at Liberty Tree. So if you can't get a reservation at one, try the other. As far as I'm concerned, this is the best place to eat in the Magic Kingdom; Thanksgiving every night with all the classic fixings. Considering it is all you can eat, this is definitely one of the best deals for a meal in MK.

Loud, inside space. The salad was okay, the proteins were very disappointing. The pot roast was over done like jerky, and they tried advertising Hormel ham loaf as “smoked pork.” Sorry Disney, there’s a huge difference. This borders false advertising. The dessert was okay but we asked for coffee with our dessert and it was cold. After paying that much, I expected a better, all around dining experience.
It was good but not worth what it cost you.
An excellent family style dining option. Great food and service.

This is one of our favorite restaurants at Disney! It’s served family-style (all-you-care-to-enjoy), and we’ve consistently had great meals here. It often gets overlooked since it’s not a character dining experience, but it has become a must-do for us—at this point, we make a point to have dinner here on almost every trip. Service can be a bit hit or miss. Our last few visits were excellent, but on our most recent trip, our server was difficult to find at times. That said, the overall experience and quality of the food keep us coming back. If you haven’t tried it yet, it’s definitely worth checking out!

Came here for lunch during one of my park days with my friend. My last name is Rodriguez and the person who walked us to the table was speaking Spanish and I told her that my friend didn’t speak spanish (wanting her to do the spiel in English so my friend could understand because tbh I didn’t understand half of what she was saying) and she just nodded her head and walked away after the spanish spiel. The food at Liberty Tree tavern was tasty it’s basically like thanksgiving dinner. The garlic rolls were probably the best part and the gravy and stuffing. There wasn’t anything amazing other than the toffee cake dessert, except neither my friend or I had room for it! So tragic.
Delicious food served family style and all you can eat. They are wonderful about dealing with food allergies and the servers are very attentive.

Liberty Tree tavern in Disney World Orlando was a terrific family friendly all you can eat buffet. The food was delicious and hot. The buffet was large with lots of choices. There was something for everyone especially for picky eaters. I loved the pot roast with gravy and mashed potatoes. The desserts were great.Our hostess was very accommodating and welcoming.
A solid standby for families in search of classic American fare, the tavern serves up quality food with quick service.
Wonderful place to bring your family when at Magic Kingdom. Plenty of food, deliciously prepared and great service.
Gustavo, ótimo atendimento
Comida boa, lugar legar e o Gustavo nossa atende foi super gente boa.
Excellente serviço e atendimento. Comida deliciosa! Ray nos atendeu com muita eficiencia e gentileza!!

Top 10 restaurants of my life. If you asked me whether I wanted to go to this restaurant or one of Gordan Ramsey's flagships, it'd honestly be a 50/50

The valet person today made me feel very uncomfortable. He mentioned before that I am messing with his tips. This is the 2nd negative encounter with the same valet guy. The staff was informed but never seem to care. You better come with your luxury vehicle that day and in a suit or else you will be treated like trash.
Atendimento simpático. Serviço excelente e se você olhar de fora nem tem essa presença impactante.

Just wow to Kabooki!!!!! Been here twice now and just getting to reviewing this spot. Let me first start with the staff! Great service from start to finish. Our server Michelle was very nice and offered good input to our questions about the dishes. We also had the honor to talk with Chef Henry Moso- we had a great conversation about the sushi and he even presented us with a dish. Grateful and delighted! kabooki's quality and execution of the dishes are a work of art! Both times we sat at sushi table and watched all the sushi chefs doing their magic was a great show. We started with the hamachi carpaccio and the beef carpaccio and both were chefs kiss We had the bluefin tasting which was great progression of variety of bluefin. Mauro Truffle, Kona Kampachi, leche de Tigro were tasty unique options. The use of micro greens and flowers was really pretty besides being tasty!! Definitely worth checking out!!

A solid 8/10 Japanese restaurant with a fantastic vibe for date nights. We ordered sushi and sake, and everything came out pretty fast. The highlight of the night was definitely the eel roll—unbelievably good! Interestingly, they also have roasted duck here. Even though I didn't try it, the ducks hanging in the display looked so mouth-watering. I’m already planning my next visit to try it out, but I heard you should pre-order the duck in advance. Highly recommend!

My first visit today was a mixed experience. I sat at the bar for lunch, and it took over 5 minutes for someone to greet me. After that, I waited almost 10 minutes before bothering the sushi chef to find me a menu (also I needed his help getting chopsticks/tableware later). The house warm sake was so bad that I didn’t finish the bottle (and I usually get two)… I have no idea what was served, but my standards for sake are low. It took almost 30 minutes for my classic sushi roll (1 order) and nigiri to be served. Thankfully, the sushi was very good.
Marvin!!!!! If you know you know.

We went her for my daughter's graduation night from UCF. It was a 10 pm reservation. The menu has excellent selection. We tried many items and all were delicious. The service was great and so was the atmosphere. It was a little cold in the restaurant, but maybe that's to keep the sushi chill. We loved it and will visit again.
Everything we had was so flavorful! Great date spot and great food

I'm not sure what I was expecting, but it wasn't this. I mean it's tucked away in a strip mall that sits kitty corner to a Target and across the street from a Longhorn. But as I walked in, I said "oh this is swanky." And it was quite possibly the best sushi I have ever had. Until tonight I didn't know that fish could be sweet. 🤯 The flavor layering was so on point.... I'm just mad I haven't tried it sooner. Will definitely be returning on the regular.

Beautiful Modern Restaurant. Limited Parking. Friendly and Professional Staff. Limited options on food. Food was amazing. I pretty much ordered all the cold tasting. The Truffle I wasn't a fan. Everything was amazing. Ribs were great portions. Drinks were so good. Great Vibes. Dress Fancy. Also just a noticed that plating the food was odd. Maybe a long plate not a bowl for the sashimi. Overall, great location for drinks, a gathering or a date.
Chef kiss

My favorite sushi restaurant in Orlando, I’ve been to many Micheline star restaurants, but Kabooki is the one I always want to come back to, I love their variety, flavor combinations and service. The bartenders team was top notch tonight even though they were busy they provided a really good service. The only unpleasant thing I’d mention is the valet. The parking lot is quite small, so valet service doesn’t really feel necessary. Also, the attendant came across as overly pushy for tips, which felt a bit uncomfortable. Otherwise, everything was amazing 🫣
The only sushi place that is consistently delicious every single time. And we’ve probably been there 30 times.

Ive never felt so uncomfortable before at an establishment. I overheard Gabriel, who I think is the manager, talking disgustingly about some of the female patrons. Commenting on their bodies and stuff that I cant even include in this review. Nobody ever said anything, everyone went along with it. If you're a woman or someone with a child, dont come here. The servers were amazing and the food was fine. Just be weary of Gabriel because I am fully convinced he's a predator.
Delicious and fresh! Knowledgeable and friendly staff.... Still my favorite after several years.
Removed the Yuca appetizer for no reason, otherwise good.

My friend works here. He's been trying for months to get me to come here but we (wife and I) live in Jacksonville so it's a hike to get here. But let's me preface this by saying...THANK YOUUUUU!!! OH. MY. GOSH. There was a hickup with my reservation but Gabe handled it amazingly and was still able to get us seated. Looking at this place from street view you'd probably look past it. It's not flamboyant but it still stands out in it's own unique way and while the outside doesn't look like a 5 star restaurant the inside will blow you away. From the bar to the open floor plan and the music. You instantly feel like you've stepped up in class from other big name "5 star" restaurants. Our waitress Day is outstanding shes very attentive and pays extra close attention to detail. She's been super helpful in laying out how to navigate the menu what her takes were for the food and all just above and beyond I wish I could give her all of the business she deserves! The tables here are quite comfy and a suitable height. The seats are actually really comfortable too! I got to experience Shen's garden (cocktail) and right then and there I knew this place was about to blow me away! It's master Shen's own cocktail but my gosh it's pure nirvana! We ordered quite a section from the menu and everything was just hit after hit. My wife HATES sushi and we got the LV roll and ended up ordering another she loves it that much! We ordered the stone shrimp it was outstanding the flavor had a nice little…

The valet individual came into the restaurant and pushed my arm to tell me to move my car. I don't feel comfortable being pushed as a customer especially if I came to pickup a large order. I understand their isn't much parking space in the lot but there was no need to push my arm. When I came outside, he said I will make sure your car doesn't drive anymore next time you come here. I asked for his name and he said "I don't need to tell you my name!" I said "There is no need to touch your customers." He proceeded to push my shoulder this time and I moved out the way. My wife took a picture of him and I just decided to walk away. This took time for me to right this review as I am very surprised by the valet individuals behavior. The kabooki sushi employees are always great and patient. I hope this doesn't happen to any individual again. Hence the reason for this detailed review. I will leave a Better Business Bureau review as well so the valet individual can be told how to properly interact with customers. If the exact date and time is needed for camera review, I will be glad to provide the information.

The food was really good. But the service was not that great. During my omakase there was multiple times I had to wait 5-10+ mins for the next course. Due to the chef that was preparing my Omakase having to help the staff prepare food for dinner rush. I understand why they tried to change the reservation time. But as being a chef myself. They should have brought in another chef to accommodate my omakase. Now the atmosphere was kind of nice but not the greatest for an Omakase.
Best Sushi! Erica was amazing!

We visit the location twice a year for my and gf's bday, and have been the last couple years. Every time has been great experiences. Location has valet parking services. Gf has dietary restrictions but does not have issues ordering. Nice drinks, I enjoy the carpaccio and tuna sushi options.
This was a great lunch spot with authentic Cuban cuisine and super nice staff. It's one of a very few restaurants open on Tuesdays in Mt. Dora.
Regular stop for us when we visit town. So many things on the menu look great! I want to try everything. It’s hard for me to resist the Garlic Cuban Sandwich and the beans & rice.
The services is 10/10 , bartender Camilo amazing and waitress Edwin very professional and knowledgeable about food ,we recommend 100% , good food times

As a former South Florida/Miami resident of 30 years, who has also been to Cuba, I have to say this is some of the BEST if not THE BEST Cuban Food/Latin I've EVER HAD. The mofongo with Oxtail in Creole Sauce..just Magical... Boiled yuca in garlic sauce, OUTSTANDING, Breaded Chicken Cutlet and Arroz con gandules (pigeon peas), Phenomenal, the friend plantains, PERFECTION... from appetizer to dessert 10 out of 10... make that 100 out of Ten!! Oh and do try the Guava n Cheese pastries for dessert... chef was gracious to send them out for us because we loved the food so much!! A Fan for LIFE!! Oh and GREAT SERVICE TO BOOT!!! And last...THE PORTIONS...I came starving and tried my best to finish my meal and barely made it halfway.
Food is great, and the servers are friendly

I’m Cuban and I recently moved to DeLand from Miami. We decided to go with my wife and father to Las Palmas to celebrate Father’s Day. We decided to drive for 50 minutes over to Mt Dora because the only Cuban place in DeLand is not what I consider really authentic. I knew by looking at menu, this was going to be a good place. We started with the croquetas and mariquitas, both were very good. I had the Vaca Frita and my wife had the roast pork. Both dishes are staples of Cuban cooking and were right on. Just like my mom used to make. The boiled yuca was very good and portions were very generous. We finished with flan and mango cheesecake which were both delicious and Cuban coffee that had the perfect amount of sugar. The restaurant was very busy but the service was fast considering how busy it was. Special thanks to our server Vanessa who did a great job. She was pleasant and attentive. We’ll definitely be back.
Great ambiance, food delicious.
Really good food, great service. Pretty good prices.
The food is always good. The atmosphere pleasant.
Great food

This is my third visit and the worst experience. I ordered churrasco expecting a good dish, but it wasn't the best. It was overcooked, it seemed like leftovers from the day before, and the plantains weren't fresh. On the other hand, the rice was good. The service was terrible. They refused to remove an insect that was flying over the food. Awful service.
una comida espectacular y un servicio de excelencia

Came to have lunch and a pleasant experience and was extremely disappointed. Was seated outside as requested, waited about 10 minutes before having a drink order taken. Ordered drinks and food at the same time. Watched 2 other tables get seated and food delivered before I got up asking about our food. Our order was simple and half the food was pre prepared. Still waited 10 more minutes for my food. As a Cuban, food was sub par at best. On top of that after waiting over 45 minutes for my order, the waitress, which so happened to be the "manager", gave me a free 5 dollar dessert to make up for the terrible service. That did not cover ruining my afternoon. Once the FULL bill came I asked for it to be discounted be 15 dollars. The owner which was on site refused to see me and kept sending employees out. The owners needs a lesson on business management and customer service bc nobody should have to wait 45 minutes for food and not even be told once that the kitchen is backed up. All in all a terrible experience and was even threatened with the police when I argued a discrepancy with the bill due to the terrible service and extremely long wait time for some pre-made food. I will definitely never be recommending this place nor coming back here again. It's too bad that this review took a third of the time to answer then my actual service in the restaurant and the sad part is that even if you were slammed packed nobody came to my table and say hey we're busy your food's going to be a…
$7 for two tostones.? You should be ashamed to yourselves. Most over priced Cuban food I’ve ever had.

I have been coming here for years. I always ordered the pork chunks with onion, black beans and rice and plantains. There is less pork now than in the past and the onions are pre-cooked and sauteed instead of cooked fresh to order. The onions are very mushy now. Last week they were over salted. The Margueriteas are great and Ali did a great job.
Best chicharones.
Fantastic

I went in and came away very disappointed with the quantity of food served for the high prices . I ordered rabo encencido with a cost of $34 and ropa vieja for around $25 and both portions were so small that I would never go back again nor I recommend it to my family and friends.

Food was over cooked.and took forever to get although the place was fairly empty. Cook got the order wrong delivered wrong sides in two out of three meals.The server was nice and efficient and apologized. The problem is in the kitchen. It was very noisy with a child screaming periodically through our meal. With so many choices in Mount Dora we won't return.
Great Cuban restaurant. The food was amazing. The service was great. The only issue was that they don’t allow firearms or weapons in the restaurant. That will keep me from going back.

The food has changed from non assuming and functional plating to more Instagram-y. The mofonfo, for example. Instead of getting the usual half circle of mofongo with your choice of stuffing, it now comes in a "pilon", a mortar and pestle style. Its looks pretty, but you have to dig the actual mofongo out from under and end up with all the toppings on the side. The stuffing which is now more like a topping, what's generous but the actual mofongo did not feel to be as much. The service, the friendly, was painfully slow. A meal for three consisting of two appetizers, three mofongos and one dessert took two hours. 4:15 - 6:15 or so, which was not even peak dinner time. The restaurant is always pretty loud, but its par for the course with many Hispanic restaurants.

Not very good all around. The restaurant always seems busy, so I took it as a sign the food must be good. In all honesty, the food didn't look or taste fresh like it was made the same day. The flavor of some of the food did not taste like it was supposed to which added to my suspicion that some of the food was not fresh or out dated. We also had to swat flies the entire time we were at the table. The service was also lacking. We waited a while to have our drink and order taken and we didn't see our server again until it was time to pay for our food. The server didn't ask how our food was or even say thank you or bye when we checked out. Between the atmosphere, food, and service, we will not be back. All of us had disagreeable stomachs after eating there. We were not the only people that had issues with the food or trying to find someone to give us the check and pay.

Love this place! The food is impeccable! The sticky ribs were my favorite dish of the evening.. Everything else was fresh and the chefs techniques were showcased on every dish. Our server Mackenzie did a fantastic job creating the experience and making our sons 13th birthday special. Thank you!
I thought the east colonial location was unbeatable until I went here. Amazing sushi, best in FL. Cant stop coming here, would have happily paid double
The spicy tuna roll is the best I’ve had in Central Florida

I honestly do not have a single thing to critique. Starting off there was a strong thunderstorm causing a torrential downpour and our son was sleeping so we could not go inside. They were able to move our reservation an hour and if we were able to come in earlier take us in, which we ended up doing. Sandra, our waitress was incredible and very transparent when we were looking for recommendations. Food was phenomenal, very fresh, unique, and delicious and great ambience as well. We ordered four rolls, sticky ribs (most tender thing I have ever had), and the ube cheesecake totaling $100.
Fresh, unique cuts of sushi
absolutely amazing experience. Kaylee, our server was very knowledgeable and was able to give us great recommendations.
Dinner with a friend

This place never disappoints! From the service, the drinks the food, everything was amazing! We had the sticky ribs 12/10! The octopus, carpaccio, and crispy tuna, all amazing! Ube cheesecake was PHENOMENAL

Absolutely one of the worst dining experiences I’ve had in Orlando. The food was decent at best, but the service completely ruined the night. The female manager working tonight was shockingly rude, dismissive, and unprofessional. What made it even worse was being told things that were clearly not true just to avoid taking responsibility for the situation. Instead of resolving issues respectfully, she came across arrogant, confrontational, and dishonest. For a restaurant that tries to present itself as upscale, the management acts like customer satisfaction means nothing. We felt unwelcome the moment we raised a simple concern. No apology, no accountability, and no professionalism — just attitude and excuses. There are far too many better restaurants in Orlando to spend your money at a place that treats customers this poorly. I will never return and would strongly discourage others from going there.
Amazing sushi!! The moving things on top of the shishito peppers weren't alive, but sure freaked me out when out on the table!!!

Food was pretty good and waitress was great, but it was an odd experience. I was eating alone, so I sat at the sushi bar. There were three sushi chefs, but none of them addressed me at all and when I tried to order, they said I needed to order my sushi from the waitress. Very confused as to why they had sushi bar seating at all. Additionally, their pricing is per piece, not per 2 pieces of nigiri like everywhere else, which I knew going in and is fine. However, the cuts of fish were about 1/3 of normal. Overall, for how highly rated this restaurant is, I was not impressed at all. Would not return.
We travel 45mins to enjoy sushi here and it’s always such a treat. Thank you.
Probably the best sushi we’ve had in our life, and we’ve been to Japan! Quality of the fish was incredible 👏
Nothing fancy other than the price. It's so dark you cant see what you are eating. Very few options in the menu. Service was ok but I won't come back.
They charge a 5% take out fee. No clear mention when I ordered.

The food here was actually quite good — everything tasted fresh, well-prepared, and you can tell they use quality ingredients. I really enjoyed the flavors and presentation, and the kitchen clearly knows what they’re doing. However, the atmosphere was a major downside for me. It was extremely loud throughout the entire visit, to the point where it was hard to have a normal conversation. For the price point, I was expecting a much more comfortable and enjoyable dining environment. Because of that, unfortunately, I don’t see myself coming back. Great food, but the overall experience didn’t match the cost.
Lots of sushi and other options. Enough veggie options. It is in the back corner of the strip mall and so could be hard to find from the street but thanks to the strip mall parking, plenty of parking
Overrated. Limited menu items. Will not return.
The service was amazing. Foods are so tasty
Always an incredible experience! Food and drinks were delicious, service was great, and as always the sushi (xo) was great!

I’ve been to this restaurant 3 or 4 times now and it is hands down the best sushi I’ve had in central Florida. The chef’s specials, to the rolls and of course the ube cheesecake!…everything has been delicious! The service and drinks as well are always on point! Highly recommend.

My wife and I eat a lot of sushi when we travel and this spot was top 5 for us. The Sashimi was fresh, high-quality, and impeccably sliced and served at the optimal temperature. Nigiri was perfectly seasoned for a balanced-bite. We had three rolls as well, all incredibly tasty. I’m posting pictures of our drinks and desert to add to reviews. All of it delicious. For saki lovers, there is a solid selection to choose from. The restaurant location was a bit odd, but you forget that once stepping inside. It seems this place could be transplanted into the JW Marriott and hold its own just fine.

Great service from Jade! We had the brussel sprouts appetizer, miso soup, a sashimi plate and a nigiri chef assortment. The cheesecake is fantastic, it is a chocolate cheesecake with whipped cream and meringue. We were greeted warmly by the hostess when we came in and offered a choice of two tables. We really appreciate the excellent customer service and the craftsmanship that went into the sushi. Our entire experience tonight was better than expected! Went back again a few months later and again had terrific service and food. Real Japanese sushi and sashimi. We ate at the bar this time so we could watch them make the sushi. We actually went twice this week. We had one great dessert, chocolate cheesecake which was different from our last visit, but just as delightful. We had tiramisu the second night and the flavor was very unusual compared to other tiramisu we have had, so do t recommend that for dessert. We love the ambiance of the restaurant though it's definitely noisy. The manager, hostesses and servers go above and beyond to make dinner a truly special experience. Great place!
Nice staff atendent
Awesome Salvador Flavor
Lo mejor de 2 mundos..... PR y SV
Everything is amazing in this place, affordable and employees very friendly !!!
The best

All these years visiting Florida Family, this was the 2st time to eat there, all the while the family has been eating here for years! My lunch was great! The good looking young lady that took our order was phenomenal! The gentleman serving our order to us was extremely polite and nice ! I ordered the picture meal, DELICIOUS!
We had , 3 pupusas “ revueltas con chicharrón “ And a horchata. It was super good! Would definitely come back again! Thanks.
Trato excepcional, comida riquísima, ambiente agradable y tranquilo. Me encantó mucho, gracias
Always come here with my wife and daughter because we love it. Food tastes good and staff is super nice. We really love this place
Amazing food and service and huge portions. Best Spanish style tripe soup I’ve ever had and top tier papusas. Very much looking forward to coming back every time I’m in town.
Excellent service and food

I love pupusas and I usually go somewhere else but today I was near here and I was like might as well try them. First time trying them and i was very disappointed. They took 20-25 mins to bring 5 pupusas out and it was just us and another table. When they came out everything was tasteless. Did not enjoy any part of the service, not the food, the sauce nor the coleslaw. Will definitely not be going back here.
Absolutely delicious food and awesome service. I had the flan and it was super good.
Love this place ❤️ everything is great I've been goin here 20 some years ❤️
Great food and customer service! Prices are also good.
The BEST TRIPLETA IN THE WORLD. 100% recomended.
The food is delicious, best pupusas in town . My wife had the cuajito and it was wonderful. The best is the service they treat you like family

We ordered the Salmon Sandwich and the Carmela at the Lake Mary, Florida location and both of these were the best we’ve ever tasted at a Jason’s Deli. We definitely had the “that hit the spot” feeling tonight!
Deja and staff were wonderful! Our meals came out as ordered and delicious! 100/10 recommend !

This place had problems with the accuracy and timeliness of their orders in the past, but now that Ms. Nicole works here, it’s one of my favorite places to go! She is thorough and very careful with allergies, and always super kind!
The food was good. Forgot to take a picture of my sandwich but the strawberry shortcake was so pretty and tasted fresh.

Atmosphere got a 3 Star because even though the salad bar was beautiful and very clean and organized, they had 3-4 booths that had piles of dirty dishes. If they didn't have all the dirty dishes, it would get a 5 star. Loved the Salad bar and soft serve ice cream machine.

This was the first time I've visited this particular Jason's Deli location. It was clean, had good service, and good food. It's a bit pricey for what you get, but then again where isn't it expensive these days, right? I ordered the "Reuben the Great," managers special. The Reuben was good but small, the chips were chips, and the pasta salad was just ok. The free ice cream (self serve) may have been the highlight!

Decided to stop in this location (Lake Mary, FL) on a whim. Ordered the combo with the ranchero wrap. Girl at register couldn't understand a simple question of "who do we tell what type of chips we want?" While waiting for our take-out there was a girl by where they are making the food talking EXTREMELY loud about personal issues. Had to listen to her complain about her family. How her mother did everything for her brother(s), how her mother wouldn't take her to games/practices, how her mother is a hypocrite, etc., etc. Don't want to listen to that when out trying to enjoy our day. We weren't even that close to her and could hear her very well. On one of the seat waiting for take-out there was trash from Dunkin Donuts and somewhere else on the chair and nobody cleaned it up. Was told a few times it shouldn't have taken as long as it did to get our food. When handed our food the woman mentioned a different sandwich so, we asked her about it and she looked at us like we had three heads and annoyed. We got "well it's whatever sandwich you wanted with the pot pie soup" in an annoyed voice. As for the food, it's wasn't bad but barely any chicken. The wrap was not "wrapped" and most of the ingredients fell out. Made a mess to eat. But feel the amount given on the wrap not worth the price or a trip back.
Very consistent. Love the salad bar.
Love their roster beef, service is kindly and patient.
Clean, good food

Saturday May 2nd, 2026 my coworkers and I ordered from here. One of my coworkers suggested we split a moose. After splitting the moose into two I just happened to take my spoon and get the bottom rim of the cup. The moose has chocolate chips in it so I expected to bite on something hard. Estuve allí con mi familia, que acababa de llegar de Colombia ese mismo día. Éramos 8 personas en la mesa y quien comenzó a tomar nuestro pedido fue el propio manager del restaurante. Sin embargo, solo tomó el pedido de 3 personas y se retiró de la mesa sin terminar de atendernos. Poco después llegó una mesera, quien tuvo que volver a tomar el pedido completo. Le explicamos que el manager se había ido sin terminar de tomar la orden, y ella amablemente intentó disculparse por la situación. Más tarde comenzaron a llegar los platos que el manager había alcanzado a ordenar inicialmente y, después, los que la mesera había registrado nuevamente. Esto generó órdenes duplicadas y varios platos repetidos. Cuando explicamos lo ocurrido, el manager se acercó a la mesa, pero en lugar de disculparse o reconocer el error, simplemente nos dijo que los platos no podían devolverse porque ya estaban facturados. Su actitud fue muy altanera y poco profesional, especialmente considerando que era el propio gerente del restaurante. No tuvimos problema en pagar la cuenta, aunque el error no fue nuestro. Lo que realmente dañó nuestra experiencia fue la falta de atención, la ausencia de una disculpa sincera y la actitud del manager durante toda la situación. Es lamentable, porque una buena atención al cliente puede marcar la diferencia incluso cuando ocurren errores.

The bathroom was well equipped and has a Japanese-style toilet with heated seat and bidet (if you’re into that kind of thing). The small room with few seats makes the experience more immersive and intimate if you’re there with someone else. Cons: The first downside would have to be ambiance. Although the experience was enjoyable, I wouldn’t say it was exactly what I expected for fine dining. The music selection was a variety of different genres including rap, country, pop, etc. The omakase room is lightly decorated, not much to look at besides the food being presented. Chef Mark. For starters, the vibe of this place was out there with very eclectic music including multiple Eminem songs, theme song from Giligen’s island, notorious BIG, country music, reggae, r&b, some electronic. It's like they had the playlist on random. It didn't have a theme that generally accompanies a fine dining restaurant of a particular food type. Then there is the "Live nudes" neon sign in the main room. I expect this in a hip sports bar, not a Michelin starred restaurant. The service was just average. Nothing special. No welcoming by name for a dining room that seats only 8. No recognition of two birthdays celebrating there. No recognition of dietary preferences that they ask about during the reservation. Then there is the issue with the chef Mark. He was engaging in a bunch of topics that didn't interest me much like stuff related to TV shows, weed, lots of F bombs and came off like he was trying to be cool. It seemed really juvenile to me. We’ve been loyal customers of La Catrina for years — easily 50–60 visits — and it used to be one of our favorite spots in Ormond Beach. Unfortunately, the experience has changed significantly. It really feels like management has shifted to the son, and the entire service culture has declined with it. On our most recent visit, the service was almost nonexistent. Our fajitas came out flaming hot, but we waited so long for tortilla shells that everything was cold by the time we could eat. I even asked the manager directly, and all he said was “They’re coming” before walking away — no follow‑up, no urgency. Our server barely checked on us the entire meal. What made the experience worse was hearing staff make unprofessional comments about customers, including remarks about people’s age and appearance. That’s something we never experienced here before, and it created an uncomfortable atmosphere. The food is still good — the kitchen continues to do their part — but the service and professionalism have dropped so far that it overshadows everything else. We truly hope the original management steps back in and restores the level of customer service this restaurant used to be known for.

If you’re looking for a spot that delivers both quality and quantity, this place absolutely nails it. The portions are huge—come hungry or plan on taking some home—and everything tastes like it’s made with care and consistency. What really stands out, though, is the old-school charm. There’s something special about a place that hasn’t lost its identity over the years. You can feel the history the moment you walk in, and that kind of authenticity is hard to find these days. It’s easy to see why this place has stuck around for so long. Longevity like that doesn’t happen by accident—it comes from doing things right and treating customers well. Lazy Moon delivers a pleasantly relaxed dining experience, particularly on a Monday when many restaurants can feel either overcrowded or lacking in energy. The atmosphere strikes a comfortable balance between casual and inviting, making it an enjoyable place to unwind after a long day. The food itself is satisfactory and consistently enjoyable, though it does not attempt to be especially sophisticated or culinary-driven. Rather than focusing on innovation or upscale presentation, Lazy Moon succeeds by offering straightforward, generously portioned fare that is both reliable and satisfying. While those seeking an elevated or gourmet dining experience may find the menu somewhat unremarkable, the quality is solid and the offerings are executed well. What stands out most is the restaurant’s laid-back character and accessibility. It provides exactly the type of experience many diners are looking for at the start of the week: comfortable surroundings, decent food, and an unpretentious environment. Overall, Lazy Moon earns a strong 4 out of 5 stars for delivering a dependable and enjoyable experience without trying to be something it is not.

This was our second visit to Lazy Turtle Riverfront, and somehow it was even better than the first! The atmosphere here is absolutely unbeatable—relaxed, welcoming, and with some of the most beautiful and soothing views of the Intracoastal you’ll find anywhere. Whether you choose indoor or outdoor seating, the waterfront scenery alone is worth the trip. Our server, Matthew, provided excellent service and made another great experience even better. Friendly, attentive, and personable without being overbearing—exactly what you hope for when dining out. The food continues to impress. We have yet to order a single thing that wasn’t delicious. The ahi tuna tacos are an absolute must-order, packed with flavor and consistently outstanding. And if you’re an oyster lover, do yourself a favor and try the East Coast oysters. They’re some of the best we’ve had and are offered at a fantastic price. Between the incredible views, great vibes, excellent service, and consistently amazing food, Lazy Turtle Riverfront has quickly become one of our favorite spots. We will definitely be back again and again!

We tried the lobster bisque, blackened mahi mahi Reuben, soft shell crab sushi roll, and island creamy rigatoni. Everything was delicious and well seasoned. ATMOSPHERE: The clear view of the water was stunningly beautiful, and we even saw dolphins jumping in the distance, which made the visit extra special. We didn’t sit outside, but we could see there was live music, which added to the fun atmosphere. If you haven’t been to Lazy Turtle in a while, definitely give them another try. We really enjoyed it and would absolutely come back!

I also appreciated the mini gym, which had everything I needed for a quick workout. The food was another highlight! Breakfast was delicious, and the Tiki Bar served wonderful meals and drinks. Blew every expectation out of the water! Last Saturday, my partner and I wanted to treat some friends to a decent mean after having had helped us move into our new house. Also, with my birthday in a couple days we wanted to find a place for our small celebration. Little did we know we were about to have one of the best dining experiences any of us had in so many years. And we do not say this lightly. Between 3 of the 4 in our party we have a collective 50+ years in the hospitality industry. After having had been sat, we were greeted by our server Jen. She was attentive, humorous, honest, and informative. Between her and her team of runners and bussers, we wanted for not. Fresh plates and silverware with each turn. The team did not miss a beat. The cocktails we delicious; well crafted works of care, perfectly balanced, pushed out by an unseen(only because we were sat around the corner from the bar) bartender that was quite skilled. The food was exceptional. A mix of perfectly elevated classics, like a flatbread with home made chili crisps, and modern approaches to dishes, like the crab dip topped, panko fried avocado that provided a beautifully silky bite with the perfect layer of crunch. But the real star of this often overlooked gem that is Luke's was the people. The Manager on duty, Emily, made sure to stop by our table, make us feel welcomed and inquire what brought us to Luke's. She ensured, along with Jen and team, that we were made to feel like we were the only ones…

The restaurant offers excellent food, attentive service, and a pleasant atmosphere, all worthy of a 5-star rating. However, it is important to note that prices can be quite steep. Unlike some other locations, this establishment does not provide lunch specials; rather, they offer recommendations that mirror the dinner menu prices. During my last visit a few years ago, there was a $40 meal for two special, which has now increased to $70. Additionally, the popular $5 take-away pasta option has been removed from the menu. This significant price increase raises concerns about the overall value, particularly when you could enjoy a lunch special at the Capital Grill for a similar expense. Maggiano's is great for those special occasions but now for your weekly go to place. I assume the prices now reflect tourism and convention traffic. If that was ever to go away, this restaurant would have to adjust prices.

Stopped in on a Sunday evening for our first visit to LongHorn, and overall we had a very good experience. The food was good across the board. The ribeye ordered medium was a little overcooked, but no big deal, and we did not find it overly spiced like some others mentioned. The ribs were definitely solid, a very good portion, fall-off-the-bone tender, minimal fat, and the BBQ sauce was good. The Tonion was good as well, though a little bland without the sauce. Fries were great. The service though was outstanding. Our server, Jessica, seemed to have back-to-back large tables, and the restaurant was starting to get pretty busy, but she did not miss a step. She greeted us promptly, was very patient and intuitive, sent drink refills without us even asking, and checked in with us several times. There was a slight delay with our food being delivered, but she kept us in the loop the whole time and never left us wondering where our food was. The food runner was also great. He was clearly busy as well, but still took the time to make the experience better, joked around a bit with the kids, and was very patient and friendly. Overall, very good experience and good food. We would definitely go back to this location. I was in the restaurant business for over 20 years in one way or another, and the service we received here is exactly how it should be: friendly, prompt, and efficient.

5/5 Stars (A+ Grade) — A Must-Visit for a Real Taste of Buffalo! If you are craving an authentic, flawlessly executed Beef on Weck, you don’t need to buy a plane ticket to Upstate New York. Just head straight to downtown Melbourne, Florida, and find a table at Main Street Pub. This place is the real deal, and they earn a well-deserved, absolute 100% A+ score. The Star of the Show: The Beef on Weck For the uninitiated, the Beef on Weck is a legendary staple born in Buffalo, New York, in the mid-19th century. Legend has it that a German baker introduced the unique roll, and a local pub owner realized that loading it with salty meat would keep patrons thirsty for beer. Main Street Pub honors this tradition perfectly. The key to the sandwich is the kummelweck roll (often pronounced kemmelick), which is topped with coarse kosher salt and caraway seeds. Main Street Pub uses incredibly fresh rolls that strike the perfect balance of savory and salty. Here is what sets them apart: They don't skimp on the meat: They pile the roast beef sky-high. They are not cheap whatsoever; it is loaded up generously. The Au Jus: The beef is incredibly tender, and the au jus sauce they serve with it is phenomenal—rich, savory, and perfect for dipping. The Beer: To wash it all down, they have an excellent selection of ice-cold draft beers on tap that pair beautifully with the salty, savory goodness of the sandwich. The Vibe and Atmosphere Beyond the incredible food, Main Street Pub is a fantastic…
