Earlier that morning, I called IHG to extend our stay by one day and was assured the reservation would remain continuous. That information turned out to be incorrect. Instead, we had two separate reservations, which significantly prolonged an already lengthy check-in process. At $23, it wasn't worth the price. Our bill was about…

The Shores Resort & Spa definitely deserves one. From the moment we arrived, the experience started off on the right foot. We were able to check in about an hour early because our room was already ready, which meant we could drop our bags and get straight to enjoying the beach. We were welcomed with a complimentary glass of champagne, our son was given a small beach ball (a simple gesture that meant a lot), and everyone greeted us with genuine smiles. Just a heads up—they do collect a $200 incidental deposit, which covers things like your resort fee, parking (self or valet), and any other charges during your stay. We booked the Cabana King Poolside Room, and if you’re planning on spending your vacation outside, this is absolutely the room to get. Walking out your private patio and being just steps from the pool and only seconds from the beach is hard to beat. Was the room itself the newest or most modern? No, it’s a little dated. But honestly… who cares? If you’re booking this room, you’re not coming here to sit inside watching TV. You’re here for the pool, the beach, and the ocean. Everything in the room worked exactly as it should, and anytime we needed anything from Guest Services, someone was there almost immediately. That’s the kind of service that matters. One thing I…

We recently stayed at The Shores Resort & Spa and overall had an enjoyable experience, with some minor disappointments. The biggest surprise was how upscale and welcoming the property felt inside. The lobby is beautiful, with elegant lighting, a candy shop, and a small market that gave the hotel a unique personality. The entire property smelled exceptionally clean, and the hallways always had a pleasant scent. Rather than feeling like a sterile hotel, it felt warm and comfortable—more like a home away from home. Our room was extremely spacious, and the mini fridge stayed impressively cold. We also loved having a balcony with a wonderful ocean view. The pool deck was attractive and well-maintained, and the tiki bar staying open later in the evening was a nice touch, even though we didn’t personally use it. The downstairs restaurant and bar also looked very nice. There were a few drawbacks. The air conditioning never quite got as cold as we would have liked, and with no ceiling fan in the room, we ended up purchasing a box fan during our stay. The television also felt too small for the distance between the bed and TV stand, making it difficult to comfortably play our Nintendo Switch. The fire pits around the pool were a great feature when available, but they weren’t always operating, and it was often difficult to find an open spot. We also noticed guests frequently leaving used pool towels around the deck. As a couple traveling without children, the pool area was a bit busier…

We stayed at The Shore Resort for the first time after seeing it advertised on Instagram, and the reality didn't match the marketing. We booked a "King Cabana Suite," but it's a standard hotel room, not a suite. The bigger issue is that the cabana rooms are not equal, and you don't get to choose. About five of them open directly onto the pool with a deep porch, a padded sectional sofa, and a couple of loungers — exactly what you'd want when traveling with young kids you can watch from your porch. We got Room 101, tucked at the far end of the property. Our porch faces nothing but another rentable cabana, so other guests looked straight into our room with zero privacy. Instead of a sectional we had a tiny love seat that barely seats two and no loungers at all. We ended up dragging loungers over from the pool deck ourselves and then having to shoo other guests off our "private" porch. At check-in I asked if anything else was available and was told no — and that I wasn't the first guest to complain, but that ownership wasn't doing anything about it. We told the front desk at check-in we had more than two people, but no one mentioned that the pull-out sofa bed would be a problem. It's easily 20+ years old, with a thin (maybe 4-inch) mattress that's stained and has terrible exposed coils — we honestly looked at ordering an air mattress from Amazon. On day two I asked about it and was told they had a mattress topper. The "topper" is essentially a second mattress, which tells me…

I recently booked a stay at The Shores Resort & Spa to celebrate a special occasion with my wife, specifically selecting this property for its large balconies and their romantic "Yes" moment package. While the hotel has great potential, the execution was a compounding series of disappointments that completely ruined the surprise I had planned.||The Positives||To be fair, the stay started on a positive note. Upon our initial arrival, the parking attendant and front desk staff were incredibly friendly, and the lobby boasts a classic elegance. We also genuinely enjoyed the proximity to the beach, the large balcony space, and the fireside s'mores in the evening.||||The Breakdowns & Disappointments|| **The Failed Romantic Package:** ||I booked a specific package meant to include chocolate-covered strawberries, champagne, roses, and a $25 daily resort credit. When we walked into the room, there was absolutely nothing there. When I went to the front desk, I was told there was no daily credit on our booking, but they promised to send the rest up. The strawberries and champagne arrived quickly, but the flowers were missing. After texting the hotel's customer service number, I was initially told flowers weren't even part of the package. They finally backtracked, admitting they *were* included but simply weren't available, and offered to refund the package price. The entire surprise I wanted to provide for my wife was completely doused.||||**Room Cleanliness & Maintenance:** ||We knew…

​I am usually not one to write terrible reviews, but our stay at The Shores Resort & Spa was completely unacceptable. For a resort that markets itself as a premium oceanfront destination, the lack of basic cleanliness and maintenance was shocking.||​The issues started right in our room:||​The Bedding: To our absolute horror, there were literal blood stains on the blanket. It makes you question whether the linens were even washed before we checked in.||​The Furniture: The living area was completely rundown. The couch was old, sagging, and covered in mystery stains, while the ottoman was totally ratty and torn up at the corners. It looked like it belonged on a curb, not in a resort room.||​The Balcony: We were looking forward to enjoying the ocean views, but the outside cushions were completely covered in bird poop and clearly hadn't been cleaned or swapped out in ages.||​The lack of housekeeping standards and attention to detail is appalling. A nice view cannot make up for a room that feels genuinely unsanitary. We will absolutely not be returning. Do yourself a favor and book elsewhere!

We also shared the cauliflower and Brussels sprouts appetizers, and both were delicious. What truly made our evening special, though, was the exceptional service. We were warmly greeted by Aria, who took the time to explain the menu and help us understand the different offerings. As visitors from Toronto, Canada, that personal touch was greatly appreciated. Jennifer then took our experience to another level. She was simply out of this world! She was incredibly attentive, answered all of our questions, and made sure my family was well cared for throughout the afternoon. Although she offered us a variety of wines and other alcoholic selections, we don’t drink, so she thoughtfully recommended several mocktails instead, which was such a nice touch. We’ll only be in Orlando for a few more days, but thanks to Jennifer’s amazing hospitality, we will definitely be back before we head home. Outstanding food, exceptional service, and a memorable experience all around. Highly recommended!

Steak was served cold. Menu items listed as “shareable” are ridiculous in size and are barely enough for one person to try. Ordered roasted golden beets “shareable” and this turned out to be 4 slices of beets with a touch of sauce. Nothing you can share there. Trout was grilled and very dry. Wonderful service but food can be better somewhere else

My daughter and I had such a great experience with Troy! He was funny, attentive, and incredibly careful with all of my allergy restrictions (and I have a long list). He made us feel welcome and truly made our experience memorable.

Billy our server was great! This was our first time there and it was for a big party celebration. Since it was early evening and a Saturday, it got packed real quick but the food is really good. We had a ceaser salad with blackened salmon and it was big enough for me and my husband to share. Great vibes, but it did take longer than expected for our entree. We will be back to try maybe during the week as they do get packed. But all in all, it was a lovely place to dine with family and friends.

I had an amazing experience during a recent business trip to Orlando. The food and service were great!! A special shoutout to Jennifer (pictured!!), our waitress, who was truly the best of the best!! She was super attentive and friendly! I would 1000% recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Orlando, and I will definitely be returning the next time I’m in town. Thank you to Jennifer and the entire team for such a memorable dining experience!
Did the early happy hour. Chicken and the dare appetizers wear good. Lots of wine choices.
Frozen espresso martini yes please!!! It was delicious!!! Food was excellent! Service was ok! The restaurant is beautiful!! Id highly recommend you make a reservation!

I would like to express my dissatisfaction regarding a situation I recently witnessed at your restaurant. While waiting in the reception area, I observed a person who had come to pick up a delivery order for a customer. Since I was standing very close to the host stand, I was able to clearly hear and see everything that took place. Initially, the staff informed this individual that the order would take a few more minutes. The person accepted the explanation and waited patiently. However, after approximately 20 minutes, they returned to ask about the status of the order and were told it would take about 10 more minutes. During this interaction, I noticed that the reception staff were not particularly friendly and came across as rather dismissive. After waiting the additional time, the person returned once again to inquire about the order. By then, they had already been waiting for nearly 40 minutes. Instead of receiving a clear explanation or solution, they were simply told that the order could take even longer, without being given any specific timeframe. It was obvious that the individual had become frustrated and eventually left upset due to the lack of information and consideration for their time. What stood out to me the most was the apparent difference in treatment. As a customer, it was concerning to see that someone working as a delivery driver seemed to be treated as less important than customers dining inside the restaurant. Delivery drivers play a vital role in the…
Our server Jennifer made all the difference! Been here many times so the food is always great but her service and attention to detail really stood out this time. Thank you!!

Sixty Vines is great spot for dinner. I have visited multiple times and typically get the pork chop. The wines also pair very nicely with the food and the wait staff give solid recommendations. The environment is also very nice. They have also taken my gluten allergy very seriously, as a celiac they have repeatedly assured all proper steps are taken to ensure it’s safe to eat. Not a lot of restaurants do that, so I am very appreciative!

A few of us went here on Sunday after church. We had Shineka as our server and she was amazing! We thoroughly enjoyed her professionalism, knowledge, and pleasant demeanor. Her food suggestions of The Breakfast Club, Egg White Frittata, and the Salmon Salad were great! I have added some photos. Thank you, we will be back!

Booked a reservation with ease a week in advance for my birthday dinner at 6:30 pm on a Sunday evening with 16 guests. My party and I had an EXCEPTIONAL TIME at the Sixty Vines Winter Park location from the moment we were seated, to our departure. Our server was INCREDIBLE as he also took care of another large party right next to us. He was so kind, attentive, and precise in everything he did for us. THANK YOU SO MUCH for your care. It made my birthday a sweet blessing. I ordered The Bright Side mocktail, the Burrata, the Campanelle pasta, and the Olive Oil Citrus Cake. Everything was a 10 out of 10. My guests commented more than once what a beautiful vibe Sixty Vines has and how much they enjoyed the diversity of menu selections, which met a variety of dietary needs. This was a wonderful place to come to and celebrate my birthday. I'm so glad I chose this establishment.

We had a great experience at 60 Vines last night! We sat at the bar, which had the perfect atmosphere for a date night. The food was delicious - we loved the meat and cheese board and the short rib pasta. The bartenders were attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable, offering great recommendations throughout the night. Troy, in particular, provided exceptional service. We’ll definitely be back and would highly recommend it to others!

Arrived to a welcoming smile from Samuel the host. Food was excellent along with the atmosphere. Jennifer our server was superb and very professional. Meals arrived quickly and drinks were always filled on time. Looking forward to visiting again!
Jess was amazing!!! She was the most personable and accommodating and doing it all by herself!! Great drinks and vibes! She deserves the best!!!
Our bartender, Jess, was amazing. She was doing it all with no help and minimal wait on the drinks. We will be back!!!! 🤍

Server was nice. Food choices were eclectic as were the non wine choices. They have vast wine choices. The burrata was great as well as rigatoni and steak frittes. The kitchen appeared to send the food out slower. But it was tasty when it got to the table.

60 Vines in Orlando is one of my favorite spots, and I personally prefer the Winter Park location. The ambience is much more enjoyable, and the noise level feels more controlled compared to the Sand Lake location, which I find can be a bit too loud. The food is absolutely amazing. I highly recommend the swordfish, pork chop, salmon, or rainbow trout. For appetizers, I always get the olives, and the grilled sourdough bread or grilled ciabatta is a must both are incredible. The hospitality and service at the Winter Park location also feel noticeably better. Overall, it’s a great dining experience and a place I truly enjoy going back to.
We had the cheeseburger pizza, chick parm sub, Italian sub and the cheese steak eggrolls. Everything was great just like the reviews
I liked the pizza it was reasonably priced and the staff was very price to me.

Came here on a whim with my son. The pizza and cheese fries were great. We tried the in house ranch worth the .75 cents. If you want good food without breaking the bank def worth a shot. Oh and the restaurant is surrounded by nice atmosphere and has outside sitting with chill vibes.
Amazing as always! The food is great, the restaurant is clean, and the staff is always friendly and helpful. This is our new "go to" spot for pizza and wings!

Jersey Pizza Snob here.. 10 years in living here in FL. SLAM Pizza is the best I've found in the area. I drive 30 mins one way, passing 5× other pizza joints to pickup from SLAM. It's as close to home as your gunna get.

Great flavors & quality ingredients. Dough is hand tossed right in front of you! The chili cheese dog is like if a meatball sub & chili dog had a baby - unique but tasty. Service is fast. Ideal for takeout or dining in.

When we tried to call 10 minutes later upon realizing the missing order, they put the phone off the hook after picking up and hanging up immediately. It was close to closing time, but still just not acceptable. We try to support local, and have given Slam a lot of business over many years, but this just gives Slam a bad name. Casual spot on the water. Food and service were very good. Went on a Monday so it was a little loud with karaoke going on.

Absolutely delicious meal! we had a few drinks to start with "Sunset Grand Margarita" we also had the "Mahi Mahi and Sunset Burger" both Amazing! coupled with a Beautiful Sunset it was a perfect moment!
Nice waterside café. I ordered potato skins and shrimp Ceasars salad. Yum!

I spent weeks researching where to do my first tandem skydive because I wanted facts, not hype. I’m terrified of heights and safety was my absolute top priority. If you read nothing else in my review, read this: Skydive Sebastian is the absolute safest, most professional and fun place to dive in the state of Florida! From my very first phone call, the team was completely transparent. Morgan answered every question I had about safety, credentials, and procedures, and even invited me to come tour the facility and watch operations before deciding whether to jump. That level of openness immediately inspired confidence. I was paired with Ian who is USPA certified (as all Tandem Instructors are), has over 30,000 tandem jumps, is head of safety and an instructor. You can’t get any better than that! As terrified as I was, I knew I was in the hands of the best of the best! Throughout the experience, it was obvious that safety isn’t just something they talk about—it’s woven into every single aspect of the operation. Every check, every procedure, and every instruction was handled with professionalism and precision. I also chose the full photo and video package because I wanted proof that I actually jumped out of an airplane! There was absolutely zero pressure to purchase it—it was entirely my decision. I’m so glad I did because Liam, my videographer, and Ian with his hand cam were fantastic. They captured every moment perfectly and made the experience even more memorable. It’s easy to…

I strapped this dude named Johnny to my back n pulled him outta th plane behind me. He then did all the work and let me just enjoy th scenery. He was100% professional but also had a great sense of humor. He even pulled off some cool maneuvers when i asked him. I highly recommend th experience. I compare it to sex w a playboy bunny. Didn't last long but it is unforgettable. If you haven't been then DO IT !! If you have been then i don't havta tell you DO IT AGAIN !!

Awesome way to start the day, we will be back soon!

The tandem team is always on point with safety protocols and the scheduling/ administrative staff is knowledgeable and helpful. If you are new to skydiving and want a fun atmosphere with a strong focus on safety, I highly recommend reserving a spot with them.

EXTREME fear of heights and falling here! I only went because it’s been a lifelong bucket-list item for my husband so we booked this skydive for his birthday. Everyone, including the other jumpers on board was so incredibly welcoming and supportive, and really helped me to move past my fear and enjoy the experience. I can’t believe I’m saying this but I actually want to do it again now! I definitely recommend SkyDive Sebastian for Florida skydiving. Best skydiving view ever!

A hidden gem near Millenia that absolutely delivers. From the moment you sit down, the experience feels relaxed yet refined — warm lighting, attentive service, and a menu that goes far beyond typical sushi spots. The miso soup was clean and comforting, a perfect start, followed by crispy, golden gyoza that had that ideal crunch without feeling heavy. The real standout is the fish quality. The sashimi was incredibly fresh, buttery, and beautifully presented — you can immediately tell they don’t cut corners here. Specialty rolls are creative without being overwhelming, and everything tastes balanced, not over-sauced like many places. Service was fast, friendly, and genuinely welcoming — the kind of place where you feel taken care of without it being forced. For the quality, the pricing is very reasonable, which makes it even more impressive. There’s a reason this place consistently gets strong reviews — many guests highlight the freshness of the fish and elevated rolls and the friendly service and relaxed ambiance . If you’re in Orlando and want reliable, high-quality sushi without the hype pricing, this is an easy recommendation. I’ll definitely be back.

At the drive throu me and my family ordered 3 cherry limeades, 1 diet cherry limeade, and 1 tot with cheese. When we pulled through the diet cherry limeade was not marked. Robbie gave me exceptional service, he is always in a great mood and treats me with respect every time I go . He makes sure my food is perfect as well as the things that go with my meal . Much respect thank you for giving me an enjoyable experience every time I come through .

alisa was amazing great service

Alisa took care of me beyond my expectations!! I definitely highly recommend this location. Staff was friendly and fast . Alisa made my experience the best experience I’ve had at that location in a long time.
Alisa gave me the most amazing service I've had in a while . Hands down great and fast service here. Highly recommend you come to this location.
Had the combo plate with a little of everything. The meat was juicy and tender; ribs and chicken just fell off the bone. The best part was the grilled corn on the cob. Sweet and juicy!

Absolutely horrendous service. The place is a gem!! Everything I had was amazing. The waiter Jerry was really attentive and kept our drinks filled and the food came out quickly.
Free parking, too much food, and a great atmosphere. They even serve your dog!!!

The service here was fantastic- the waitress went above and beyond chatting with us and being super friendly. The food was okay- the mac and cheese was so fake it didn't even taste like mac and cheese, and the ribs were a little dry. My friend had the burger and said it was nothing special either.
Love the outdoor seating, was visiting on vacation and glad I stopped. We eat gluten free and they were very accommodating to it. Food was great!
Our waitress was very nice and the food was very good. Our waitress answered our questions and was helpful on avoiding food allergens. They were also kind and brought my service dog water.
This place has some really good BBQ food, the location is great and really cool atmosphere when sitting outside. Anytime I have been here, the customer service has always been great as well.
Good always

Stopped by Slow and Low on Cocoa Beach for dinner, Hailey took wonderful care of us while provided us with great recommendations that we loved. Restaurant was bustling with energy and had great live music. Next time will ask for lean brisket if i am able, other than that everything was amazing! We will definitely be returning next summer!

Slow N Low is misleading, especially the high review rate, those people must be drunk. The food was below par and tasted as if it was not only cooked yesterday, but was underwhelming given the price and menu description. I was highly disappointed after spending my money there and will definitely not be returning.

We ordered thru DoorDash. With BBQ you just never know what you’ll get. The burnt ends had way too much sauce, they tasted ok but too wet, I would suggest they leave off the sauce, great burnt ends don’t need it, let the meat shine. The baby back ribs (no sauce) were very tasty, good smoke. Definitely only sauce on the side, lets the meat shine. The brisket was a little too much toward pot roast (wet) even with (no sauce), rather than a great brisket with just the right pull, but it had good flavor. The pretzel was a bit on the overdone side, which we actually like, so good job! Didn’t care for the broccoli salad, very strange taste. Garlic mash was good. The fried okra was ok, as was the collards. Enjoyed the key lime pie. Overall it’s ‘ok’ just not great BBQ.
Hard n dry ribs. Burnt turkey leg and tasteless sides . Very expensive n disappointing.
A must! Love the outdoor patio! Just all around wonderful!
do not eat here
Delicious food and friendly staff. They had a separate event going on which created a bit of distraction for staff but otherwise it was great.

Halli served us last night and did an incredible job! She learned both of our kids names quickly and connected well with them as well as provided everyone with very friendly and engaging service. To food was excellent! Their smoked chicken was phenomenal and I really liked their mustard bbq sauce. Overall, I loved the vibe and service. Will definitely come back next time I’m in Cocoa Beach.
Loved this place. Ate outside. The brisket is fantastic. Jerry took good care of us.

We stopped here after a day at the beach. The worst bbq we’ve ever had, the brisket tasted like it was sitting in a warmer all day and the sides were terrible and bland. The only ok thing was the cornbread muffins. We got one of each dessert and those were bad too. It was very disappointing. We spent a lot of money for 6 people that felt like it was wasted.
The food was AMAZING. We come from MA just for this meal. Ally is godsend. Would highly recommend

The meat for the ribs and wings were delicious, although 3 ribs and 5 wings for $26 is a little pricey. They could really work on the flavor of the sides, I had the mashed potatoes and greenbeans (I had 2 bites of both and didn't finish due to blandness). My wife had the mango smoothie which was so delicious that we ordered 1 to go. She had the chicken sandwich which was so so (5/10) and the coleslaw which was a bit better (7/10). Would definitely come back but would love to see more work put into the sides. Jerry was our server and he was extremely attentive and made the experience much more fun, very nice guy and great server. Overall it is good.

Outstanding BBQ. We have tried most all of it and are never disappointed. It is a must stop whenever we are in town. It is the only BBQ place we have found that is a regular stop because it is the only commercial BBQ that rivals mine.

Came in on a Monday night and we sat at the bar. Katie, the bartender was awesome! We started off with wings (On Monday’s it’s $1 wings) we got the extra spicy buffalo with garlic. The wings were decent, they are smoked which leaves a good flavor but consistency was definitely chewy. Next we tried the rack of ribs. Again these had a good flavor but they still had the membrane attached making them chewy and messy. The pulled pork with the chipotle BBQ was the best, nice and tender. Mac and cheese was pretty plain, nothing to really rave about same with the coleslaw and tater tots. Onion rings were nice and golden brown with a good crunch. Lastly the cornbread muffins were very very dry, we took one bite decided that was all. The atmosphere was very chill considering there were only 2/3 tables and we were the only ones sitting at the bar. It seems they have good weekly deals such as the $1 wings and $3 margs after 6pm on mondays. There is also a 10% military discount. Overall this place is a solid 4/5 stars. Service is good and the atmosphere is chill, food is good just some minor flaws :)
Nice place!! Baby Back ribs-out of this world, juicy, tender, not over cooked.

I thought about this review for quite a while before posting it. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing. The music was extremely loud and never let up, which made the atmosphere feel overwhelming rather than enjoyable. We considered leaving early, but we had already ordered appetizers and decided to stay. Those took about 45 minutes to arrive. When our beers were brought out, they appeared to have been sitting for some time before reaching our table. We mentioned it to the staff, but our concerns were dismissed. To be fair, the food itself was good. However, the service was poor, and the overall atmosphere made it difficult to enjoy the meal. In the end, we finished dinner, paid what felt like a premium price for the experience we received, and headed back to our room. Based on this visit, I can only give it two stars.

Saw reviews online and gave it a try. We were disappointed. Food came out warmish, except for the pretzel it was hot, and very good. We had the combination plate. BBQ Chicken and roasted corn were the best two items on the plate. If you go order the pretzel it's huge. I wouldn't make a special trip. We did go on a rainy Sunday so maybe it was the day we chose to go.
Baby back ribs, chicken wings must have.the best.

This is the 2nd day we’ve been here in a row - which is saying a lot because my husband is a bbq snob! Madi our server has been absolutely phenomenal- and the food was AHHMAZING! The Mac & cheese topped with pulled pork & fried jalapeños was worth the 5 star rating. Pair the amazing food with the kick butt service - it’s definitely a place worth visiting more than once! (And the voodoo juice…icing on the cake!)

If Luke Bryan were visiting Viera, this would be his spot!! Local BBQ with great outdoor and indoor vibes, plenty of bourbon and whisky, tons of TV’s and amazing staff and food! And Ofcourse the best Happy Hour in all of Viera! Wednesday is ALL DAY HAPPY HOUR… amazing BBQ…..and if you like wings these are wings down THE BEST WINGS ANYWHERE!!

So good! This place is back!!!!! The food was amazing!! Finally good BBQ at a good price. Nick the Bartender was cool as well knew the menu and was very cool to talk to him! Will be back. Thanks for the food that was worth every penny in this economy!
Decent BBQ & prices. Happy hour has COLD draft beer. Friendly bar staff. Live music last Friday I went.

Stopped by for a few snack(just appetizers). Had the wings with mild sauce. The taste was great! Smoky with a hint of hot sauces. I would have gone hot but some places call their hot mild, no this is mild with no real heat. Could've used a few more sticks of celery but no biggie. Next up, burnt ends. A different waitress or runner dropped them of and said " Good choice, they are delicious." They were ok. Seemed like they were good at one point but this was towards the end of the night. A few were hard cubes of meat. Dry and just a bit too hard to eat. It was like getting that dry piece of turkey at thanksgiving that you choke down with your drink. Sauce was ok. The waitress asked if I wanted to replace them with something else and declined. The place was empty by 930 which was a surprise for a Friday but the staff was still attentive. I'd try it again.

All the food was bland and dry. Fish spread. Fried green tomatoes. You need to add horseradish to the horseradish dip. Brisket was like pot roast. Baby back ribs bland and dry. Sausage was bland and overcooked. The spicy slaw was simply disgusting.You need to introduce your chef to some seasoning.

Don't waste your money if you're looking for good BBQ. I went based off reviews and boy was I wrong to do that. This food was SO bland. Fried green tomatoes had zero seasoning, fish dip was crazy dry (and weirdly sweet), the brisket was HORRENDOUS. It was more like an overcooked pot roast- zero moisture, zero tenderness- just chewy, dry, flaky meat. My husband said the spicy slaw was literally inedible. The only thing I enjoyed was the coleslaw (which was as basic as it comes but at least it was good after adding salt and pepper). Service was fine, no complaints there; but for the cost of food these days, leaving more than half behind sucks.
Awesome BRISKET ! and dessert are homemade!

Amazing bbq and great service by Bella. Our server should be the #1 trainer as her skills and timing were perfect, checked on us frequently without our meal or conversation. Perfect brisket, Brunswick stew, and service. So much better than Sonny's and tastier, less pricey, and 100% better sauces and sides than Crydermans ever thought of.
Great spot! Great Q & amazing service. Staff was incredible. Stopped in a few times while in town for a pint and sandwich and the staff even remembered my name.
The food and service was SO GOOD! Shout out to Mady- she was so attentive and kind. We will definitely be back!

The only place I have ever gotten Burnt Ends that were what I'd hoped for. So many places give you chewy steak bites basically. The barbecue sauce was so sweet and sticky and just perfect! The potato salad was a little mustardy I thought, but when I tried it I loved it. The potatoes are not too big, so you get a lot of the good stuff. You have to try the Fried Bread Pudding. The Key Lime Pie was good, but I forgot to say no whipped cream so I can't really judge. Not bad though. The waitress was really cool and responsive, and the owner came by to chat for a while. We sat outside. Really nice experience. Looking forward to going back.

Gluten free choices and a great atmosphere! It was such a great place to have an extended lunch to catch up with my friend. The manager and the server were attentive and checked in without making us feel like we had to leave. It was the best lunch. Great food and great service. Highly recommend! I didn’t get the bread since I’m GF but my friend did. I thought the bun was cool.

Fantastic meal! The BBQ was excellent and our server was too. (The atmosphere was very loud due to a boy's sports team - otherwise it would have been 5 stars all the way.)
Excellent food, good service and a bargain!

Met the owner who was very nice and explained the Chipotle sauce which is good or I would have never tried it as typically not a fan but it was awesome and our favorite. Ribs were super good and tender. Will go again and highly recommend.

As a chef and restaurateur with 30 years of industry experience, I can confidently say this establishment deserves a much higher rating. The wings were exceptional—perfectly seasoned with a balanced dry rub, expertly crisped, and finished with just the right amount of smoke. I opted for the sampler to test the range of the menu, and every item delivered. ​Barbecue is a notoriously difficult craft to master, but this team is doing it right. With great food, attentive service, and very reasonable pricing, this is a local gem worth supporting. I’m glad I bypassed the larger chains like Ford’s Garage for this authentic experience. Don't miss out.

Great food, comfortable to sit and chat while eating.
Food is very good and presentation appetizing. Very friendly and knowledgeable wait staff. You need to experience it to really appreciate it!

The food is alright but the price is so reasonable and the service is so fast that whenever I don't feel like going to Cracker Barrel I'll come here. I gave 40% gratuity because my waitress was excellent. Every worker seemed to work hard and kept a good vibe. That is hard to find.
Quaint restaurant with amazing food and great staff. Will definitely be returning and recommending to others
Very impressed! Food came out so fast. Prices are unbelievably affordable. And many options to choose from. Coffee is great. Service was phenomenal every server was so kind and fast.

A must Stop and Chew Location! Just as expected breakfast and brunch served off of a wide selection of dishes. Made to order we tried the Philadelphia Cheese steak, Ruben, eggs over easy and spectacular sausage gravy.
If I return back in under a week for a breakfast sandwich!!! You know they’re delicious
The food is great! Cafe is always packed so most times it's just better to get your food to go.

What a great find! Very clean, friendly service & awesome food. They definitely seamlessly work as a team. Kylee cheerily greeted & sat us. Her recommendations were spot on from the iced coconut mocha to the avocado chorizo special. There are so many new dishes, to me, that I’m definitely gonna try & make my way through the menu.

We came in to visit our hometown; have been to this Cafe before, on a weekend when it was packed. Always great service! We went unexpectedly today (Monday around 8:45am) and I tell you- FAST! But still so friendly!! I was shocked; felt like I was in a twilight zone. I think my family of 3 got in and out in under 25 minutes! Food (& specialty coffees) were excellent as always!!
This is such an awesome cafe!! The servers are VERY attentive and pleasant. The food is EXCEPTIONALLY delicious and VERY reasonably priced. Great food in a quaint area!
This was my first time eating at this establishment. The service was superb! The food was delicious!! We received our food very quick!!! The staff is amazing!! I highly recommend!!!
Super crowded but so worth it. Great food. Excellent service. Reasonable prices
It was very nice to see so many helpful people. The place is amazing. Good food, nice people, nice clean establishment. I think its one of the best places around.

Went here for the first time for breakfast, coffee was delicious and strong. I had eggs over hard and bacon, everything was cooked very well. The atmosphere is very open which makes it very loud, that was my only gripe. Servers were very friendly and attentive even on a busy morning. I'd come back, but maybe not for a date just because it is so loud.
Very good breakfast, sitting outside was a nice morning breeze, wait staff was excellent!! Grits are so creamy and delicious!!
Our favorite breakfast place. Excellent service. Top notch food. From unlimited healthy smoothie choices to gravy smothered entrees you can't go wrong here.

We had never been to this Cafe before but we were in Ft Pierce and decided to have lunch there. My husband had the sirloin steak rice bowl and he said it was the best lunch he's had in awhile! And we go out to eat a lot! The service, food and pricing were excellent. We'll go back again soon!
Great brunch spot! Drinks and food came out quicker than I was expecting, and service was friendly and smooth. The french onion pork panini and bananas foster chai hit the spot!

The meal and the service were excellent. Jermaine, our waiter was so good.

Enjoyed my meal a lot! Jermaine was a great waiter & service was great🙌🏾

Sweet tea was also delicious. Joey Rodriguez was doing live music, one man band and he DID NOT disappoint - super cool to watch and voice like butter.
Dinner here was wonderful. Great atmosphere and the beignets stole the show!

Genuinely shocked at how quickly our food was ready. We didn't have to wait for a table. Our server was incredibly kind. 4 stars on the food, because it was pretty basic or standard. Nothing stood out or had a wow factor. It was delicious, but that's what we expected. Overall great dine in experience.

Pior lugar , disparado, que eu já comi e bebi em Orlando ! Não vale a pena ! Vendem bolo de milho falando que é pão e o frango com cebola que pedi veio mergulhado no óleo além da quantidade mínima ! A huge shoutout to Byron at House of Blues Disney Springs! Thank you for making our concert experience last night so amazing. Your kindness, professionalism, and positive attitude truly stood out and helped make the night even more memorable. We really appreciated all your help—thanks, Byron! 🎶😊

Saw The Runarounds at House of Blues and they were great. Fun energy, good crowd, and a really enjoyable show. The venue was easy to navigate, and the concert had a cool intimate feel. Definitely worth seeing.

Stopped to get out of the heat and grab a bite to eat. Nachos with brisket were plentiful and delicious, as were the margaritas! 😋 Our server was on top of things during our visit, and oh so friendly!
I really love drea as a sever she’s sweet & make sures everything is great, the food was amazing.

This Japanese izakaya has become one of my favorite spots to unwind and enjoy great food. The atmosphere feels authentic—warm lighting, lively but not chaotic, and the kind of place where you can relax, share plates, and actually enjoy the experience instead of rushing through a meal. The food is excellent and clearly made with care. The small-plate style makes it fun to try different dishes, and everything I’ve had has been flavorful and well balanced. From grilled skewers to fresh sashimi and comforting hot dishes, nothing feels generic—it’s a place that truly respects Japanese cuisine. The drink selection is also a highlight. They have a solid variety of sake and Japanese beers, and the staff is always happy to help if you’re not sure what to choose. I’m pretty conflicted about this restaurant. I tend to avoid coming here because the location is a hassle—especially if you’re coming from the west side of town and have to cross Mitchell Hammock. More importantly, the wait times are consistently frustrating. It usually takes 30–45 minutes to get my order, which feels unacceptable for a fast-food spot. That said, the burgers and fries are usually very good. I do have a few suggestions for improvement. First, consider giving customers the option to choose whether condiments go on the top or bottom of the burger. I personally prefer them on top and often end up eating my burgers upside down because of this. I understand putting condiments on the bottom can help prevent the bun from getting soggy, but some people prefer tasting them first before mixing with the rest of the burger. Lastly, it would help to include the car’s location on the receipt or bag. That way, servers wouldn’t have to spend extra time searching for the correct vehicle when delivering orders. For comparison, your competitor, Steak ’n Shake, is right up the street. It’s easier to enter, the prices are lower, the food quality has improved significantly, and it typically only takes about 15 minutes to receive an order. With wait times as long as yours, it makes you wonder where customers are going to choose to go instead.

Fiddler’s Green Irish Pub & Eatery has basically become the unofficial home base of Motherfunkler at this point. We’ve recorded live podcast episodes here, closed the place down after long conversations about life/music/business/Florida chaos, and watched completely random groups of people somehow end up talking to each other by the end of the night. That’s the magic of a real neighborhood pub. Nothing about this place feels manufactured. The lighting’s a little dark, the bar always feels alive, somebody’s usually yelling about soccer, and there’s almost always an interesting character sitting three stools away if you pay attention long enough. The food is exactly what you want from an Irish pub — hearty, honest, and built to support decisions that may or may not involve another Guinness. More importantly, Fiddler’s still feels human. In a world full of places designed mainly to be photographed, this place was clearly designed for people to actually gather in. Motherfunkler will always support spots like that. 🦩

Tony’s Town Square is easily one of the worst dining experiences I’ve had at Disney, and I have been to many Disney restaurants! The disaster starts with the check-in process. It’s completely disorganized, with no meaningful seating in the lobby for waiting guests. Instead, you’re left standing around in a crowded area while staff mumble names that are nearly impossible to hear or understand. For a restaurant that serves this many people every day, it’s astonishing how poorly managed the front end is. The bathrooms are another example of poor planning. They are far too small for the volume of guests, creating unnecessary lines and frustration. Who knows the last time they were properly cleaned! Once you’re finally seated, be prepared to wait. And wait. And wait. The food takes an unreasonable amount of time to arrive, only for it to be incredibly underwhelming. The menu is bland, uninspired, and tastes more like cafeteria food than a restaurant charging Disney prices. The most frustrating part is the cost. Tony’s charges premium Disney prices for a bargain-basement dining experience. You’re paying a fortune for mediocre food, slow service, and a chaotic atmosphere. Disney is known for creating exceptional guest experiences, but Tony’s Town Square feels like a place that survives solely because of its location on Main Street, not because it earns repeat customers. There are countless better places to spend your money in Magic Kingdom. Save your time, save your money, and eat…

I took my fiancé to Texas de Brazil for Father’s Day, and unfortunately this was one of the most disappointing experiences we’ve had there. We had a 7:00 PM reservation and, after being seated, there was some difficulty finding a high chair for our baby. While that issue was eventually resolved, the biggest problem was the service from the servers walking around with the meat. The entire purpose of dining at a Brazilian steakhouse is to enjoy a continuous variety of meat selections brought directly to your table. Throughout our meal, very few cuts of meat were offered, and we spent much of our time waiting. When we requested medium to medium-well cuts, the meat we received was either extremely overcooked or so rare it was practically still mooing. Our waitress was wonderful and attentive, and this review is not directed at her in any way. She did her best and provided excellent service. The issue was clearly with the overall operation and execution during a busy holiday evening. For a bill of nearly $160, we expected the experience and quality that Texas de Brazil is known for. While we were sent home with two complimentary desserts, that did not make up for the lack of service and value during the meal itself. We have enjoyed dining here in the past, which makes this experience even more disappointing. Management needs to do a better job staffing and maintaining service standards during peak times. Paying customers should receive the same quality experience regardless of…

Most of the meat that came to our table was tough and chewy. What made it even more disappointing was that we spent most of the meal eating rice, beans, and scalloped potatoes because there simply wasn’t enough meat coming around. The biggest draw is the dessert menu, especially the over-the-top milkshakes and chocolate creations. The milkshakes are designed to be as much a visual attraction as they are a dessert, with large toppings and elaborate presentations that make them perfect for photos. The chocolate bread, macarons, truffles, and other bakery items also add to the experience, giving guests plenty of options beyond a typical restaurant dessert menu. The savory menu is broader than expected, offering burgers, pasta, sandwiches, and other comfort food options. The food is generally solid, with dishes like the burgers and larger entrées standing out more than some of the lighter options. While the restaurant’s theme is built around chocolate, the savory dishes help make it a full dining destination rather than just a dessert stop. Service is usually another strong part of the experience, with staff helping guide guests through the large menu and explaining some of the more unique items. The restaurant can get crowded, especially during busy CityWalk hours, and waits are…

When employees go above and beyond — especially right before closing — many of us would love the option to show our appreciation. Fantastic character breakfast and easily one of the best meals we've had on Disney property! We ordered the Steak & Eggs, Quiche Gruyère, and Eggs Benedict Florentine after seeing them recommended in other reviews, and honestly, every dish was a hit. The Eggs Benedict Florentine was probably the star of the table, but the quiche was a close second. We had recently tried the quiche at Cake Bake Shop and found it pretty underwhelming, so this one completely exceeded our expectations. It was rich, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. The steak was cooked perfectly, and even the potatoes and side salad were surprisingly good. The drinks were fantastic as well, especially the espresso martini-style cocktail with Baileys and Frangelico. What made the experience even more special was celebrating my mom's birthday. The characters truly went out of their way to make her feel celebrated. We noticed the interactions felt much more personal and relaxed than other character meals we've done recently. One of our favorite moments was watching Daisy Duck get down on the floor and play toy trucks with a little boy. Throughout the meal, we saw the characters taking their time with guests and creating really meaningful interactions. The combination of great food, excellent drinks, and such thoughtful character experiences made for a truly memorable morning. We would absolutely come back!

Topolino’s Terrace Character Breakfast was one of the highlights of our Disney trip! The atmosphere was beautiful, the character interactions were fantastic, and the food exceeded our expectations. The breakfast selections were fresh, unique, and delicious, making it feel much more elevated than a typical character dining experience. The characters were wonderful- engaging, fun, and attentive without making us feel rushed. They spent plenty of time at each table, and the overall experience felt magical and well-organized. The pricing for the meal itself felt fair considering the quality of the food, the character experience, and the Disney atmosphere. My only criticism is the tipping expectation. Because the meal is prix fixe and much of the experience is centered around the characters rather than traditional table service, there was very little interaction needed from our server after our order was taken. Our coffee was left in a carafe at the table, and we didn’t require much additional service throughout the meal. As a result, a standard 20% tip amounted to nearly $50 for what felt like minimal waiter involvement. That said, this was a minor drawback in an otherwise outstanding experience. We would absolutely return and highly recommend Topolino’s Terrace to anyone looking for a memorable character breakfast at Disney World.

That Little Restaurant is an absolute gem. Located at the end of the shopping center with plenty of parking, this cozy spot offers both indoor and outdoor café-style seating. The atmosphere is simple, cheerful, and beautifully decorated, creating a warm and welcoming environment. There are TVs for those who enjoy keeping up with current events, and while the tables are often full, the wait is usually not long. The food is consistently excellent, and the portions are generous we always leave with enough for another meal. Everything tastes homemade, including the delicious desserts we took home. The omelets are incredible, and the pasta dishes are amazing. In our opinion, it’s some of the best food at some of the best prices around. What truly makes this place special, though, is the service. The staff is friendly, attentive, and makes you feel like family. It’s a wonderful place to visit anytime, with something for everyone on the menu. Breakfast is served until 2 PM, which is a huge plus. Honestly, this may be one of our favorite restaurants.

The location is great, within walking distance to Discovery Cove and Aquatica, and a very short drive to Sea World. Also has a number of shops and restaurants very near by. However, even overlooking the in-room air-conditioning compressor (which seems to be present in most American hotel rooms) and associated noise, the walls are paper thin so you hear neighbours' conversations and TVs, including of they chose to watch late at night. There allso a very noisy fridge-freezer in the room. Beyond this, the breakfast is very hit & miss in its offerings and they are always running out of provisions that the single member of staff struggles to resolve in a single breakfast sitting. It was busy all the time, and we went for breakfast at a variety of times, with queues for the few waffle machines. It had a pool, which is open until late, but it is very shallow and seemingly intended more as a play area for young children than as an offering for older families, and certainly not adults. Plenty of parking but at a cost. The family suite is a good size but could do with some doors on the kids room and a few more coat hooks to dry beach towels and damp clothing. We would not go back.

I have been on hold financially while the restaurant works through the process of getting back on its feet, but it was a special occasion and we were excited to enjoy a night out as a family. Once the owner of Siam Orchid found out that I worked at Tiny Turtle, he insisted on taking care of our table for the evening. The kindness and generosity shared by Siam Orchid parallels their delicious food. We are big sushi fans and Siam never disappoints! We always enjoy a sashimi dinner loaded with high quality cuts of salmon, tuna, escarole, and other chef choices. They have rolls for everyone, cooked and uncooked options. We love the raw options and our top rolls are the Daimyo Maki Roll and the Beauty and the Beast Roll. I also love their Tom Yum Gai Soup and both the Green and Red Curry dishes. If you are looking for a delicious place for dinner, and a staple to our community, you should absolutely stop in and enjoy everything Siam Orchid has to offer!

These were just excellent breakfast potatoes and nicely complemented each of our meals. Also I appreciate a breakfast place that has tasty high quality bacon and a willingness to cook it crispy, and this place passed those tests. But the real stars of the show for us were (1) the super friendly service and (2) the dog friendly patio. Now, when I tell you it was a warm sunny humid summer mid morning, you may say what kind of idiot would choose to dine outdoors when there was plenty of room in the fairly spacious indoor dining area. Well, we had our sweet pup Max for one thing, but here's the amazing part...despite the fairly brutal weather conditions, that covered patio was like a little micro climate and was totally pleasant. We’ve dined here several times, but never for breakfast. We found it to be much less busier at breakfast and barely had to wait on a table. Our waitress, Mia was fantastic. Very attentive and had great suggestions. I got the pancakes which came with a blueberry vanilla compote, butter, maple syrup, bacon, and sausage. The pancakes without any toppings were airy, but kind of dry. However when you add a little syrup and the blueberry compote, it almost just sinks into the pancake and is just the right level of sweet that I like my pancakes. The compote changes seasonally, but the tartness of the blueberries mixed with the slightly sweet hint of vanilla blew me away. The sausage was good too. It had a good sear and snap. Now the real magic is the Al Forno eggs. It’s such a unique and complexly flavored dish. They cook it in the wood fired oven. It’s sunny side up eggs with fennel sausage, spiced tomato sauce, and cheese over a layer of polenta served with grilled country bread. Zero notes. This was savory, rich, and indulgent. Everything worked together. The egg yolks mixed with the flavor of the fennel sausage and acidity from the tomatoes along with the creaminess of the polenta was simply perfection. Trattoria Al Forno has proven time and time again that their food and service is consistent and worth every penny! Quick update: We went last week and they've changed the tomato sauce they use on the pasta and pizza and I am not a fan! I knew it had cream in it as soon as I saw…

Trader Sam's Grog Grotto at Disney's Polynesian Village Resort is an absolute must-visit for anyone looking for an immersive and wildly entertaining tropical lounge experience. ​From the moment you step inside, you're transported to a vibrant South Seas hideaway filled with fantastic tiki decor and clever Easter eggs nodding to classic Disney attractions. ​The real magic, however, lies in the interactive elements. Whenever certain drinks are ordered, the atmosphere changes with special effects and cast-led interactions that make every sip an adventure. ​While it's family-friendly until eight in the evening, after that, it becomes an adults-only sanctuary perfect for enjoying a Nautilus or a legendary Zombie. It's amazing how much thought goes into the presentation and storytelling behind each of their signature drinks. The way the cast members commit to the story, combined with those fun special effects, really makes the whole experience unforgettable. It's like being part of a mini-show while enjoying your drink.

One of my favorite spots to be! It may be a small venue, but it packs a mighty atmospheric punch that can't be beat. Otherwise, there's a beautiful patio outside with a nice water feature often featuring live music as well. Don't forget to bring home one of their quality limited edition tiki mugs that are so much fun to collect, display and use at home.... goddess Uh-Oa insists🌋°o°

Walt Disney, to Victor Bergeron: "Hey. Hold my Mai Tai." For real. Trader to trader. Sam's is Vic's turned up to eleven, and then maybe even to twelve. It's got the Disney budget. This is as Polynesian Pop as it can get with the multi-million dollar budget to make it happen. Which they do. Look. If you're reading this, you know all that already. So here are your pro tips: Make a reservation. The Disney app works for that, supposedly. They'll take walk-ins. But since the space is small, expect a wait. This Taco Bell. The employees are my goats. I went inside at 10:45 PM in a JROTC uniform with nothing but agony and despair in my soul. My car had broken down, just outside the parking lot. My serpentine belt snapped. I had to rush somewhere quickly. Time was of the essence. And then, I spotted the bell. I and my friends who were in a train had already been heading here but it felt like a beacon in the rain. A symbol of hope in my hour of darkness. I turn in with my friends behind me and fly into that parking lot with pure agony in my heart for what I know has happened. As my belt has already snapped before I knew of the warnings, I knew of the sound, that awful wretched sound. I opened the hood of my car look where my serpentine belt should have greeted me running… to find it shredded. Half way down my 2004 Honda crv’s engine bay. I throw my hood back down in anger and open the GEICO app for a tow truck desperate now as it is so late at night. An hour is the estimated time it will arrive to my location. I’m now desperate in this foreign land of lake Mary where I must get home to deltona. I curse my wanting to get a crunch wrap now and go inside reluctantly with my friends. I explain what has happened to the employees and ask them “if I need to may I leave my car here overnight” fully expecting a no. To my surprise an angel among men was working that night. She heard my pleas and immediately gave me sanctuary, offering for me to stay in the parking lot if need be as I was…

Wishing you the same superb experience I had during my stay🤗

This hotel is a solid option for a quick, budget-friendly stay, but it definitely has some tradeoffs. My partner and I stayed here for one night during a longer Orlando resort trip, and overall it served its purpose well enough. The rooms are a bit tight, but they have the basic amenities you’d expect for a short stay. The biggest downside was the AC units. In our first room, the AC was extremely loud, to the point where it made sleeping difficult. The staff had no issue moving us to another room, which we appreciated, but unfortunately the AC in the second room was just as loud. If you’re a light sleeper, bring earplugs or consider another hotel. Outside of that, the experience was positive. The lobby has a fun atmosphere with a pool table, and the breakfast was surprisingly decent for this type of hotel. We especially liked the pancake machine. For a cheap overnight stay where you’re mostly just using the hotel as a place to sleep, you could definitely do a lot worse. I wouldn’t go out of my way to recommend it over comparable nearby hotels, but if you’re a Hilton member and getting a good rate, it’s a perfectly acceptable option.

We had a very disappointing experience today at the Boardroom photo location with Stitch at Typhoon Lagoon. We waited in line patiently, and when our turn finally came, there was nobody behind us. We were the last family in line. Each photo session was taking less than a minute, so it would have only taken a very short moment to allow my child to take a picture. Instead, as soon as it was our turn, the staff packed up and started leaving. I politely asked if they could please take one quick photo since we had already waited our turn and there was nobody else waiting. My child is only 3.5 years old and was very excited to meet Stitch. What upset me most was not that the photo session was ending, but the complete lack of empathy and customer service. My son was standing there looking at them, clearly disappointed, and they showed no concern, no apology, and no sign of understanding that they were disappointing a small child. Their attitude came across as annoyed and dismissive, and they simply walked away, telling us to come back later. I fully understand that employees have schedules and operating hours, but when a family has already waited in line, is next in line, and there is nobody behind them, a little kindness and consideration goes a long way. A simple photo would have taken less than a minute.

Tusker House is one of those places where the spectacle of the characters, the noise, the Disney gloss threatens to overshadow the food, but don’t let it fool you. Beneath the safari‑camp theatrics, there’s a buffet with real backbone. The mac n cheese, wildly off‑theme ends up being the quiet hero of the whole operation, playing wingman to everything from curry shrimp to meatballs. It lifts the entire meal, a humble floor‑raiser in a room full of distractions. And just when you think you’re done, when the sensible part of your brain begs you to stop, a fresh tray of bread pudding appears and you find yourself going back in, no regrets. Add in the African Bloody Mary. Spicy, balanced, crowned with a slab of candied bacon, and suddenly Tusker House feels less like a character meet‑and‑greet and more like a place to escape from the chaos of the park.

I had crab here before and I'm not sure if they do not have it anymore or if they don't have it on the weekdays. They have a conveyer belt that shuttles vegetables, dumplings, tofu and noodles around so it's easy to grab. I like that this restaurant labels it too so you know what it is. Everything is individually saran wrapped for cleanliness. The hot food station had appetizers such as chicken wings and spring rolls but also had cooked food like ham fried rice and a delicious fried salt and pepper jumbo shrimp. I loved it. Would definitely continue to be a repeat customer.

Most people writing these typically start with the positives but with a small amount of research it is obvious that the few positives are the location which includes the monorail and lastly the dining. The negatives, however , far outweigh the benefits of a shorter ride to MK. The biggest and most egregious issue is the noise level. We stayed club level 3rd floor and all day everyday all you hear in your room is the slamming of doors and loud tromping up and down the halls. It does not stop. Ever. So if you are the type of Disney goer that likes a mid day rest before dinner or going back to the park, I hope you aren’t a light sleeper. It truly is impossible for even a 15 minute stretch of not hearing a door slam and we pack a white noise machine when we travel and it could not even stifle it. Next is the bathroom size and shower. There is zero room for your items in the bathrooms and our room in particular didn’t have a fully functioning shower and the wall paper was peeling in the shower itself. All this to say when you are paying a premium price you at minimum expect and peaceful night sleep and a decent shower. The staff we very lovely and accommodating and honestly tried their best but the entire vibe of this resort is chaos and we definitely won’t be returning. We come to Disney almost every year and we wanted to try a new resort and it did not meet our expectations. We’ll be sticking with our usual French Quarter from here on out.

We loved staying at the Polynesian Resort. The rooms were beautiful, the pools were great, the grounds were amazing, the staff were absolutely fantastic. And the trip to MK was so easy. The biggest issue we had was for 4 restaurants on property the food was very repetitive and lacking sufficient options for vegetarians and kids (what happened to grilled cheese?). I will also note housekeeping was very delayed. We would be at the park until 3 and when we returned housekeeping wasn’t done and at that point we didn’t want them to come in as we were relaxing. Wish they had come earlier in the day. I would highly recommend the resort and we loved the tower but if you have someone in your group struggling with walking it is a bit of a trek from the main building.

There was also plenty of food options nearby or a short monorail trip away. Everyone at the rest was very friendly.

I was so excited to visit the Poly for the first time. Unfortunately the experience wasn't all I'd hoped it would be. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived, so our bags were stored .....somewhere. After waiting quite awhile for our room, still wearing our airplane clothes, we decided maybe we'd go swimming. When I went to try our luggage, no one seemed to be able to help. Luckily our room was ready within an hour of that exchange. It look at least another hour for us to get our luggage. We missed our first dinner reservation because of the delays at the property. I did find the resort to be beautiful but way too crowded. We looked forward to fireworks on the beach. All available chairs were taken well before fireworks started, so we made the best of it and sat in the sand with not even a towel underneath us. I requested a third floor room. We got a 2nd floor room. Every morning we heard loud beeping from conversation equipment right outside our window. This was not the magical vacation I hoped it would be and certainly not worth the premium price we paid. Probably won't be back to the Poly and watching social media closely before deciding if we'll be back to WDW at all.

We stayed club level at Polynesian in the Hawaii building. We arrived early and got checked in and waited for our room. After several hours of waiting in the lounge we were told my a worker Lauren if my 5 year old didn't have shoes on he couldn't come back in lounge mind you he only got out of his wagon one time im 3-4 hours. I explained to her he was special needs and we weren't just being rule breakers there was no compassion or anything helpful offered. So the remainder of the trip he never entered the lounge again because we weren't comfortable so what a way to start off a trip. The concierge couldn't help us with info about a stroller wagon pass for special needs because they said they never heard of one but the main lobby told us all about. I find it funny we got more help out of the main lobby than the concierge desk and you pay more for concierge. My family was not greeted with lais we had to go back in main lobby and ask. While this wasn't my first time here it was for some of my family. Upon the rest of the week you had people in dripping wet swimsuits and half dressed leaning over the food in the lounge and barefoot and nothing was said to them. I felt discriminated against because my child was treated unfairly. I want there to be more education given to employees on special needs children especially autistic children. This was heartbreaking that we felt shamed and were unable to take him back in the lounge, mainly because we were excited he could watch fireworks…

She didn't clock out of work, there wasn't a shift change, as a matter of fact there was a young couple seated a table away from us, that came in about 10 minutes after us that she started serving. She frequented this couples table giving refills and brought their food out promptly. We actually ordered before the young couple, but their food was out on their table, meanwhile the same waitress didn't even come to check on us or give us an update. Another lady was seated at the table next to us, she had a different server. This server had her tea out immediately, and her appetizer was on her table within 5 minutes of her tea being served. At this point i was extremely disappointed. I forgot to mention, when we noticed our wait was abnormally long, i tried to flag down the waitress as she was serving everyone else, and that didn't work. Now mind you, we have been waiting 45 min - 1hour, and everyone else around us is being served. So I went to the bar and spoke to someone there to cancel my order. While visiting Umpas Diner, the atmosphere was cute and had the small-town diner charm we usually enjoy. Our waitress was friendly, but she seemed a bit out of it during the visit. Another waitress—who I assumed might be the owner—came across as rude during our interaction. At one point I asked how they make their tea. I only asked because I personally don’t like when tea bags are boiled since it gives the tea a bitter taste, and I wanted to make sure so I could order something else if needed. The question seemed to be taken poorly, which was a little uncomfortable. We also waited quite a while for our food even though the diner wasn’t very busy. When the food arrived, most of it was overcooked. My bacon was actually great, but the sausage and eggs were very overdone. The eggs in particular were so overcooked that I didn’t eat them. I did politely let the waitress know the eggs were overdone and not edible. I wasn’t asking for them to be remade or for a discount, but nothing was offered or done to address it. Overall, the diner itself is cute, and we genuinely enjoy supporting small businesses and local diners. That’s exactly why we came in. Unfortunately, based on this experience, I had expected a bit more in terms of both food quality and service.

Our server, Jonathan, started off pleasant, but throughout the night became extremely passive aggressive and made us feel uncomfortable. The caprese salad was honestly one of the blandest I’ve ever had — just tomato and cheese with no balsamic, olive oil, salt, or seasoning whatsoever. After our appetizer, we noticed every table around us received complimentary bread except ours. We brushed it off, but shortly after, Jonathan approached the table and sarcastically said, “I heard you ladies want complimentary bread,” in a very rude and condescending tone. We were genuinely caught off guard because we hadn’t even complained — we had simply noticed it amongst ourselves. The entire experience made us feel uncomfortable, almost like our conversations were being listened to or monitored, which completely changed the atmosphere of what was supposed to be a fun birthday dinner. To be fair, the gnocchi was very good, the fettuccine Alfredo was good, and the gluten-free pizza was decent. On Facebook it looks amazing with all the handpay jackpots, but look closely at what people are playing: many are betting $10 per spin or more. A lot of familiar faces that used to come here all the time apparently don’t come anymore for the same reason. PLEASE AVOID THIS PLACE!!!

Regardless, I enjoyed this plate a lot! I was impressed by the bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls). The rice rolls were thin and delicate, but the star was the filling which had nice meaty strips of pork and chunks of papaya which I havent seen before. Also the nuốc chấm was the perfect accompaniement, a little spice, a little sweet, but mostly just savoury goodness. Lastly, our server was very attentive and polite.

But here's what really set her apart: she made us feel like the most important table in the room, and I have a feeling she made *every* table feel that way. That's not a skill you can train. Vincenzo, if you're reading this — Christina is the kind of server who turns first-time guests into regulars. It's easily one of the best dining options on CityWalk. But as great as the food was, Christine was the absolute highlight of our entire night. Her service wasn't just good; it was completely above and beyond. She was warm, incredibly attentive, and had this amazing energy that just made us feel welcome the second we sat down. She anticipated everything we needed before we even had to ask, offered great recommendations, and paced our meal perfectly. The kitchen makes a great meal, but Christine is the one who makes this place a 5-star experience. We will definitely be back to Vivo, and we'll be asking for her by name! Pros: Authentic and delicious food, great atmosphere, but Christine’s world-class service steals the show!

My husband and I visited VIVO Italian Kitchen at CityWalk Orlando yesterday, and it was truly a wonderful experience from start to finish. We both ordered the Chicken Fettuccini Alfredo - and I'm not exaggerating when I say it's the best chicken pasta we've ever had. The sauce was rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced, with tender chicken that just melted in your mouth. We'll definitely be ordering it again on our next visit. To drink, we both went with the Fragola Fresca mocktail - a sweet, refreshing strawberry cocktail that was absolutely delightful and a great complement to the meal. For dessert, we went our separate ways: I had the Tiramisù, which was absolutely divine - incredibly light and delicate, with a subtle coffee flavor and no overpowering taste of alcohol whatsoever. My husband chose the Semi Freddo, which was a smaller portion but surprisingly satisfying and filling. Both desserts were a perfect ending to the meal. And last but not least - our server Char was a true gem. She was warm, friendly, and incredibly attentive, with a smile that was genuinely contagious. She made the whole experience feel special and personal. If you're visiting CityWalk and looking for a cozy, delicious Italian dinner, VIVO is an absolute must. We'll be back!

If I could give Waffle House more than five stars, I absolutely would. My recent visit was nothing short of amazing, and it reminded me why this place has such a loyal following. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted with genuine warmth. The staff treated me like family—smiling, energetic, and ready to make sure everything was perfect. There’s something special about that classic Waffle House hospitality, and they delivered it flawlessly. The food was outstanding. I ordered the classic All-Star Breakfast, and everything on the plate was cooked exactly the way I wanted it. The waffles were golden, fluffy, and full of that signature flavor that no one else can match. The eggs were perfectly prepared, the bacon was crisp, and the hash browns—scattered, smothered, and covered—were deliciously addictive. Every bite was comforting, hot, and fresh, exactly what you want from a great diner-style meal. What really stood out, though, was the atmosphere. Even though the restaurant was busy, the team behind the counter moved with incredible coordination. They called out orders, cooked nonstop, checked in on guests, and still kept a friendly, upbeat attitude. It’s rare to see that level of teamwork executed so smoothly. You could genuinely feel that they cared about the experience they were giving their customers. Waffle House is one of those places that feels like home no matter where you are, and this visit reminded me why. The food, the people, the energy—everything was amazing.…
